- Kensei: A sword saint, a swordmaster so devoted to the way of the blade that his skill borders on the spiritual, often wandering to test himself in duels. Calm, austere and nearly legendary, he wins with one perfect stroke. Hook: unrivalled single-target swordplay, but he is single-minded and seldom gets involved with politics.
### Historical: Wild West
- Gunslinger: A quick-draw duelist of the American frontier whose reputation rests on speed, steady nerve and a well-worn revolver. He drifts from town to town, meeting challengers eager to make a name. Hook: lightning-fast shooting and intimidation, though notoriety draws trouble and every fight could be his last.
- Outlaw: A wanted criminal of the frontier who robs trains, banks and stagecoaches and rides with a gang across lawless territory. Dusty, cunning and always one step ahead of a posse, he lives by his wits. Hook: ambush skill and local knowledge, with a bounty on his head.
- Lawman (sheriff / marshal): A badge-wearing officer who keeps order on the frontier, juggling shotgun, jail cell and tense local politics. Lonely, weary and often outgunned, he stands for justice in places that barely recognise it. Hook: authority and deputy backing, weighed against corruption, isolation and violent reprisals.
- Bounty hunter: A relentless tracker who hunts wanted men for reward money, bringing them in dead or alive. Cold, patient and skilled in reading trails, he works outside the law's careful procedures. Hook: tracking and ruthless efficiency, with moral ambiguity and a bad reputation among honest folk.
- Saloon keeper: The owner of the frontier's social hub, who pours whiskey, hosts card games and hears every rumour in town. Friendly yet shrewd, he knows who has gold, who is wanted and who is lying. Hook: an information broker and neutral ground, though he must stay out of trouble to stay alive.
- Gambler: A card sharp who drifts through saloons and riverboats, winning stakes with skill, bluff and sometimes a card up his sleeve. Smooth, watchful and impeccably dressed, he reads people better than hands. Hook: charm, deception and wealth, but bad luck or a caught cheat can mean a bullet.
- Railroad baron: An industrial tycoon who drives iron tracks across the frontier, buying land, officials and hired guns to clear the way. Wealthy, ruthless and convinced of progress, he reshapes whole regions. Hook: vast resources and political influence, but he makes bitter enemies among settlers, tribes and rivals.
- Native scout: A tracker and guide, often from a local tribe, who leads army columns, surveyors and settlers through unfamiliar land, reading terrain, weather and signs. Caught between worlds, he knows the country intimately. Hook: wilderness expertise and diplomacy, with divided loyalties and the burden of broken promises.
- Snake-oil salesman: A travelling con artist who peddles miracle tonics from a painted wagon, charming crowds with patter and staged cures. Fast-talking and always ready to skip town before the truth catches up, he survives on persuasion. Hook: silver tongue and social manipulation, but no real fighting ability.
- Cavalry trooper: A mounted U.S. army soldier who patrols the frontier, escorts settlers and fights in campaigns, armed with carbine, sabre and pistol. Tough and disciplined, he endures harsh posts and uncertain orders. Hook: mobile firepower and army backing, but bound by chain of command and tied to politics.
### Historical: Renaissance
- Assassin: A Borgia-era killer who works with dagger, poison and patience, striking from crowds, shadows and rooftops at the command of princes and cardinals. Elegant and ruthless, he leaves little trace. Hook: precision kills and stealth, though he is expendable to his masters and hunted by their rivals.
- Alchemist: A scholar-craftsman of the Renaissance who studies transmutation, elixirs and poisons in a smoky laboratory, pursuing the philosopher's stone and often pleasing wealthy patrons. Brilliant yet secretive, he walks a line between science and heresy. Hook: potions, poisons and knowledge, with volatile experiments.
- Courtier: A polished member of a prince's court who wins influence through wit, flattery, fashion and elegant rhetoric. His duels are fought with rumour, favour and carefully chosen words. Hook: social manipulation and access to power, but dependent on patronage and endangered by one wrong remark.
- Condottiero: A hired military captain of Renaissance Italy who commands a private army and sells it to rival city-states, treating war as a business. Shrewd and professional, he balances loyalty against profit and survival. Hook: skilled command and negotiable allegiance, though employers fear he may seize power.
- Inventor (da Vinci type): A brilliant polymath who sketches flying machines, war engines and anatomical studies, funded by patrons hungry for novelties and weapons. Curious, distractible and decades ahead of his time, he fills notebooks with wonders. Hook: gadgets and engineering insight, with unfinished projects and suspicious clergy.
- Spymaster: A patient director of intelligence who runs a web of informants, ciphers, forged letters and double agents for a prince or republic. He sits at the centre of secrets, trading knowledge for power. Hook: information control and manipulation, though a single betrayed agent can unravel everything.
- Poisoner: A quiet and methodical killer who dispatches rivals by slow poison slipped into wine, gloves or perfume, thriving amid courtly intrigue. Patient and learned in toxins, she avoids direct confrontation. Hook: untraceable deaths and fear, but exposure leads to swift and terrible retribution.
- Duelist: A rapier specialist who settles matters of honour in disciplined, stylish combat, trained in fencing schools and sharpened by street fights. Quick, graceful and proud, he treats every insult as a challenge. Hook: precise single combat and flair, though he is poor against groups or firearms.
- Inquisitor: A religious investigator of Renaissance Europe who examines suspected heretics, banned books and rebellious thinkers on behalf of the Church. Learned, stern and politically empowered, he can ruin careers with one accusation. Hook: authority and interrogation, creating enemies among scholars, artists and nobles alike.
- Banker: A financial power broker who lends fortunes to kings, popes and merchants, controlling war and politics through credit and ledgers, as the Medici did. Smooth, informed and patient, he prefers contracts to swords. Hook: wealth and leverage over rulers, though his fortune depends on debtors' survival.
### Historical: WWII
- Rifleman: The backbone of every army, a mud-caked infantryman in a steel helmet carrying a bolt-action or semi-automatic rifle and a heavy pack. Reliable and adaptable, he holds lines and takes ground. Hook: individually modest, but strongest in squads that cover one another, and desperately short of supplies.
- Sniper: A patient marksman in camouflage who lies motionless for hours with a scoped rifle, picking off officers, gunners and radiomen from hundreds of metres. Fear and demoralisation are his real weapons. Weakness: a single muzzle flash or glint reveals his nest and invites counter-sniping or mortar fire.
- Combat medic: An unarmed or lightly armed soldier with a red-cross armband and a satchel of morphine, sulfa powder and bandages, who crawls into fire to reach the wounded. Keeps squads fighting longer and alive. Hook: running out of supplies forces brutal choices over whom to save.
- Resistance fighter: A civilian turned saboteur in occupied territory, working by day as a baker or railway clerk and by night cutting phone lines, derailing trains and ambushing patrols. Knows every alley and cellar. Weakness: informers, reprisals against neighbours, and scarce weapons and ammunition.
- Spy (SOE / OSS): A trained clandestine agent of British or American intelligence, parachuted behind enemy lines with a forged identity, a radio set and a cyanide pill. Organises resistance cells, gathers intelligence and sabotages industry. Hook: one slip at a checkpoint or a captured codebook unravels the entire network.
- Codebreaker: A brilliant, often eccentric mathematician or linguist working in a secret country house or bunker, cracking Enigma and other ciphers with pencils, punch cards and early computing machines. Wins wars without firing a shot. Hook: acting on decrypted intelligence risks revealing the secret to the enemy.
- Pilot: A daring aviator in a leather jacket and flight goggles, flying a fighter in swirling dogfights or a heavy bomber on long perilous night raids. Skilled, superstitious and living on borrowed time. Hook: speed and altitude are power, but fuel, flak and damaged engines make every sortie a gamble.
- Partisan: An irregular guerrilla fighter living in forests, mountains or marshes with scavenged weapons, striking supply lines and garrisons before vanishing into the wilderness. Backed by sympathetic villagers. Weakness: poor equipment, brutal reprisals, and political divisions between rival bands that sometimes fight each other.
- Tank commander: A grease-stained officer who rides in the turret of a steel behemoth, directing driver, gunner and loader through smoke and dust by radio and hand signals. Commands armoured punch and shock. Weakness: cramped, blind and fiery when hit, and always dependent on fuel and crew cohesion.
- Nurse: A stoic, overworked caregiver in a field hospital tent or ruined church, patching shattered soldiers by lantern light as shells rumble nearby. Her calm holds the ward together. Hook: provides healing and morale, while carrying secrets from dying men, and can be caught in a frontline advance.
### Historical: Cold War
- Double agent: A spy who serves one intelligence service while secretly reporting to its rival, living a polished lie of divided loyalty. Feeds each side carefully chosen truths and falsehoods. Hook: every meeting could be a trap, and discovery means execution, a prison swap on a foggy bridge, or exposure.
- Courier: A forgettable-looking runner who ferries microfilm, cash and messages through dead drops hidden in hollow bricks, park benches and library books. Never knows what he carries. Weakness: tailing agents watch known drop sites, and one missed signal chalk mark leaves him stranded and exposed.
- Defector: A scientist, officer or diplomat who slips across the Iron Curtain carrying secrets in his head and seeks asylum in the West. Immensely valuable and fiercely hunted. Hook: both sides want him, one to debrief and the other to silence or retrieve him, and his motives may be doubted.
- Handler: A patient, coolly manipulative case officer who recruits, pays and directs agents from behind an embassy desk or in rented safe houses. Reads people like ledgers. Hook: he must balance an agent's safety against the mission, and a burned asset often becomes expendable.
- Sleeper: An agent planted for years or decades in an ordinary suburban life, with a spouse, job and neighbours, awaiting a single activation phrase. Utterly convincing because the cover has become real. Hook: when the call finally comes, he may no longer wish to answer.
- Saboteur: A skilled demolition operative who disrupts rail lines, power grids, factories and pipelines with plastic explosives, timed fuses and mundane accidents that look natural. Strikes the enemy's infrastructure rather than its people. Weakness: needs careful reconnaissance and a clean exit before security forces seal the area.
- Diplomat: A smooth, tuxedoed attache with immunity who attends embassy receptions while quietly running agents and collecting gossip. Cannot be jailed, only expelled. Hook: his protection is his shield and his leash, and a scandal or a recall ends his usefulness overnight.
- Nuclear technician: A white-coated engineer or reactor operator who handles fissile material, test devices and warhead maintenance, and knows secrets worth killing for. Always watched by security. Hook: radiation, contaminated areas and meltdown risk make him a hazard to himself and others, as well as a target.
- Border guard: A rigid, suspicious sentry in a watchtower or checkpoint booth, armed with dogs, searchlights and rifles, inspecting papers and trunks beside a wall or minefield. Embodies the boundary between two worlds. Weakness: low pay and bureaucratic habits make him bribable, or sympathetic to a desperate family.
- Radio operator: A headphone-wearing specialist hunched over a shortwave set, tapping Morse, transmitting numbers-station codes and listening for enemy chatter. Lifeline for agents in the field. Hook: every broadcast risks triangulation by direction-finding vans, so he must keep moving and keep each transmission short.
### Historical: Prohibition-era gangsters
- Mob boss: A sharply dressed crime family head in a pinstriped suit who rules a city district from a back room, controlling alcohol, gambling and politicians through loyalty and fear. Rarely dirties his own hands. Weakness: rival families, ambitious lieutenants, and the tax man who may bring him down.
- Enforcer: A hulking, loyal muscleman with a baseball bat, brass knuckles or a sawed-off shotgun who collects debts, breaks legs and silences troublemakers on the boss's word. More intelligent than he looks. Hook: reliable violence, but a loose end if his boss grows nervous.
- Bootlegger: A resourceful smuggler who brews moonshine or runs real liquor in from Canada and the Caribbean, using fast cars with hidden compartments and speedboats at night. Supplies the speakeasies. Hook: hijackers, police roadblocks and rival gangs all want his shipment.
- Gun moll: A glamorous, quick-witted woman in a sequined dress and cloche hat, partner or girlfriend to a gangster, who knows his secrets and can handle a pistol. Far more than decoration. Hook: loyalty may turn to betrayal, and she often has her own plans.
- Corrupt cop: A beat patrolman or precinct captain who takes envelopes of cash to look away, tip off raids and lose evidence. Wears a badge but serves the mob. Weakness: a crusading reformer or federal investigation can expose him, and his masters will not protect him.
- Speakeasy owner: A charming, discreet proprietor of a hidden bar behind a barbershop door or in a cellar, with a peephole, a password and a secret escape tunnel. Serves jazz, gin and gossip. Hook: raids, protection payments and temperamental patrons constantly threaten his livelihood.
- Torpedo (hitman): A cold, professional contract killer in a fedora and overcoat who takes payment to remove rivals, witnesses and traitors, usually by pistol or garrote. Arrives unannounced and leaves quietly. Weakness: his reputation attracts enemies, and one botched job makes him the next target.
- Accountant: A bespectacled, mild-mannered number cruncher who launders illegal profits through laundries, theatres and shell companies and keeps the books that could hang everyone. Never touches a gun. Hook: his ledger is both the mob's greatest asset and its greatest vulnerability, and prosecutors want his testimony.
- Tommy-gun gunner: A reckless gangster with a drum-fed Thompson submachine gun, hanging from the running board of a black sedan to rake a street with sustained fire. Pure intimidation and chaos. Weakness: wild, inaccurate shooting, heavy ammunition drain, and a tendency to attract overwhelming police response.
- Federal agent: A G-man in a dark suit and snap-brim hat, Treasury or Bureau, who builds cases against mobsters through wiretaps, informants and undercover work. Incorruptible by reputation. Hook: he may infiltrate the gang under a false name, but a single recognised face ends his life.
### Modern: noir detective, private eye
- Private eye: A rumpled investigator in a trench coat who works out of a shabby office with a bottle in the desk drawer, tailing cheating spouses and finding missing persons. Cynical but bound by his own code. Hook: simple cases always spiral into corruption reaching high places.
- Femme fatale: A beautiful, mysterious woman who walks into the detective's office with a sob story and a veiled agenda, using charm and danger in equal measure. Rarely tells the truth. Hook: she may be victim, villain or both, and trusting her usually costs dearly.
- Police informant: A nervous street-level snitch who trades whispers about crimes and criminals for cash, favours or leniency, hanging around pool halls and diners. Knows everyone's business. Weakness: always at risk of exposure, and his information may be stale, exaggerated or deliberately false.
- Crooked DA: A polished, ambitious district attorney who sells justice, burying cases for donors while prosecuting enemies for headlines. Smiles for cameras and takes envelopes in private. Hook: untouchable legally, so the detective needs evidence, leverage or an ally within the machine to topple him.
- Cigarette girl: A bright-eyed, observant young woman circulating through a nightclub with a tray, who sees who sits with whom and who leaves in a hurry. Underestimated by everyone. Hook: a key witness or alibi, but being talkative with detectives can make her a target.
- Burned-out cop: A disillusioned former police officer, drunk on regret and bad memories, who was forced off the force for refusing to play along or for a mistake he cannot forget. Still knows the streets and old friends. Weakness: addiction, grudges and a short temper.
- Fixer: A well-connected go-between who solves problems quietly for the right fee, arranging favours, silencing witnesses and smoothing over scandals for the powerful. Knows whom to call. Hook: loyal to cash and leverage, and useful as an ally or a dangerous obstacle.
- Newspaper reporter: An ink-stained, fast-talking journalist with a press pass tucked in his hatband, who trades tips with the detective for the exclusive. Chases headlines at any hour. Hook: provides information and publicity, but a story printed too early can wreck an investigation or get someone killed.
- Gangster client: A dangerous but wealthy underworld figure who hires the private eye for a delicate job, such as finding a missing associate or a stolen ledger. Pays well and watches closely. Hook: refusing is risky, accepting means serving a master with his own hidden agenda.
- Coroner (noir): A dry-witted, world-weary medical examiner in a cold, tile-lined morgue who reads corpses like confessions, spotting poison, stab angles and time of death. Offers cynical wit and crucial forensic clues. Hook: official records can be altered, and sometimes he already knows too much.
### Modern: street medic, paramedic, field surgeon
- Street medic: A volunteer healer in a bright vest at protests and community events, carrying a backpack of saline, gauze and eyewash to treat tear gas, injuries and panic attacks. Calm in chaos. Hook: frontline care without official backing, often under threat from crowds or police.
- Paramedic: A trained emergency responder riding in an ambulance with defibrillator, oxygen and drugs, stabilising patients in living rooms, highways and rooftops before the hospital. Fast, methodical and unflappable. Hook: every minute matters, and difficult scenes, hostile bystanders and tough calls test composure.
- Trauma surgeon: A steady-handed doctor in scrubs who works in an emergency operating room, performing damage-control surgery on gunshot, blast and crash victims at all hours. Holds life in her hands. Weakness: exhaustion, ethical weight and limited blood supply when many arrive at once.
- Combat medic (modern): A soldier-healer with tourniquets, hemostatic gauze and a rifle, who treats wounded comrades under fire and prepares them for medevac. Trained to stop bleeding in seconds. Hook: must balance saving one patient with protecting the squad, and carries the emotional toll of losses.
- Veterinarian: An animal doctor with a clinic or a field kit, who treats pets, livestock and wildlife, and recognises sick creatures, diseases and poisons others miss. Gentle with the voiceless. Hook: useful for creature handling, tranquilisers and sedation, and as an unorthodox surgeon for patients who cannot visit a hospital.
- Triage nurse: A sharp-eyed nurse at the emergency room entrance who sorts arriving patients by urgency in seconds, deciding who sees a doctor now and who waits. Cool-headed under pressure. Hook: her decisions carry moral weight, and during mass casualties she must make grim choices others cannot.
- Ambulance driver: A skilled, nerve-steady driver who threads sirens and traffic to deliver patients alive, knowing every shortcut, alleyway and hospital in the district. Quick reflexes, dark humour. Hook: mobility and escape, but a damaged vehicle, blocked road or reckless chase can doom a critical patient.
- Chemical decon tech: A hazmat-suited specialist who scrubs chemical, biological and radioactive contamination from people and places with showers, tents, sensors and neutralising agents. Methodical and cautious. Hook: expert on toxins and exposure, but suit time, air supply and unknown agents limit how long he can work.
- Disaster relief volunteer: A compassionate community responder who arrives after earthquakes, floods and storms to give first aid, hand out supplies and organise shelter. Improvises with whatever is available. Hook: strong morale and local knowledge, yet limited formal training and equipment leave her stretched.
- Underground doctor: A disgraced or idealistic physician practising from a back room or basement, treating the wounded, undocumented and criminal without records or questions for cash or favours. Skilled but unlicensed. Hook: a valuable ally for fugitives, who risks arrest, blackmail and dubious clients.
### Modern: corporate fixer, hacker, data thief
- Corporate fixer: A sleek, discreet professional on a company's payroll who deals with scandals, rivals and inconvenient people through bribes, leverage and well-timed accidents. Never named in the minutes. Hook: powerful behind the scenes, but disposable if the corporation decides he knows too much.
- Black-hat hacker: A skilled, hooded intruder who breaks into networks for profit, fame or sabotage, exploiting software flaws, phishing and stolen credentials. Lives behind aliases and proxies. Weakness: one careless trace or a betrayed partner can bring federal agents to the door.
- White-hat hacker: A licensed security researcher who probes systems with permission, finding vulnerabilities and reporting them before criminals do. Often a former black hat who changed sides. Hook: knows how attackers think, but may be pressured, underpaid or tempted to cross the line.
- Data thief: A corporate espionage specialist who steals trade secrets, client lists and prototypes, using hidden drives, inside contacts and forged badges. Works for rival firms or the highest bidder. Hook: valuable information makes him a target, and getting caught means lawsuits, prison or worse.
- Social engineer: A charming manipulator who gets past locked doors and passwords by talking, posing as a repairman, executive or helpdesk worker and exploiting trust and politeness. Human nature is his exploit. Weakness: relies on improvisation and confidence, and one suspicious employee ruins the con.
- Insider threat: A trusted employee with legitimate access who is bribed, blackmailed or ideologically motivated to leak secrets or sabotage from within. Bypasses every firewall. Hook: detection is difficult, and paranoia about who it might be tears apart teams.
- Crypto courier: A low-profile carrier who moves untraceable value in hardware wallets, memorised seed phrases and cash drops, bridging the digital and physical underworld. Quiet and careful. Hook: a prime robbery target, and one lost key or seized device wipes out a fortune.
- Executive assistant: A composed, razor-sharp aide who controls the boss's calendar, calls and secrets, deciding who gets an audience and who gets turned away. Knows where the bodies are buried. Hook: a powerful gatekeeper and a potential ally or leaker, depending on loyalty.
- Compliance auditor: A meticulous, relentless investigator with spreadsheets and subpoenas, who follows the money trail to expose fraud, bribery and hidden accounts. Disliked by management. Hook: a danger to every corrupt executive, and at risk of intimidation, bribery or an accident.
- Lobbyist: A polished influence broker who wines and dines legislators, drafts favourable bills and funnels donations, shaping laws to suit paying clients. Knows everyone in the capital. Hook: access and leverage are power, but scandals, leaked emails and shifting political winds can destroy his standing.
### Modern: journalist, whistleblower
- Investigative reporter: A tenacious journalist who spends months digging through documents, interviews and leaked files to expose corruption, often at great personal risk. Driven by the story and public interest. Weakness: threats, lawsuits and burned sources, and a story that is not airtight can ruin a career.
- Photojournalist: A courageous camera-wielder who documents wars, riots and disasters up close, dodging bullets for the one image that moves the world. Carries press credentials and spare memory cards. Hook: captures evidence and exposes truth, but is caught between safety and the shot.
- Whistleblower: A conscience-stricken insider who exposes wrongdoing at their employer or government, risking career, freedom and safety to tell the public. Often isolated and hunted. Hook: holds explosive proof, but needs protection, a trustworthy journalist and an escape plan.
- Source: An anonymous informant who feeds a reporter tips, documents and background, speaking only by encrypted channels or in parking garages. Identity is the most guarded secret. Weakness: exposure can cost his job or life, and his motives may be revenge or manipulation.
- Editor: A hard-nosed gatekeeper in a newsroom who decides which stories run, how they read and when, balancing truth, legal risk, advertisers and deadlines. Backs or kills a scoop with a word. Hook: a powerful ally or obstacle, who can be pressured from above.
- Podcaster: A charismatic independent voice with a microphone and a loyal audience, who dissects mysteries, scandals and crimes outside traditional media. Fast, unfiltered and personal. Hook: can rally public opinion quickly, but lacks institutional protection and can spread rumours as easily as revelations.
- Fact-checker: A diligent truth auditor who verifies every claim, quote and statistic before publication, spotting forged documents and doctored images. Quietly protects the outlet's credibility. Hook: can validate or demolish a story, and sometimes finds a lie in the very heart of it.
- Stringer: A freelance reporter who works without a salary or safety net in dangerous regions, selling stories and photos to whichever outlet pays. Knows fixers, drivers and local contacts. Hook: gets to where official crews cannot, but is expendable, unprotected and underpaid.
- Leak broker: A shadowy middleman who trades in secrets, connecting leakers with buyers, journalists or rival governments, and takes a cut for anonymity. Operates through encrypted drops and intermediaries. Hook: a source of explosive information, but his loyalties are for sale and he can sell out anyone.
- Press secretary: A smooth, quick-thinking spin doctor who shapes a politician's or corporation's message, deflecting hard questions and burying bad news in late-night releases. Controls access to the powerful. Weakness: caught lying on camera, his credibility and career collapse with his employer's.
### Modern: special forces, PMC
- Operator: An elite special-forces soldier drilled in close-quarters combat, night raids and rapid improvisation, kitted with suppressed weapons and optics. Operators work in tight cells and trade on speed, precision and calm under fire. Hook: peerless skill, but years of secret deployments leave scars and divided loyalties.
- Breacher: The assault team's door-kicker, who opens barricaded entrances with shotguns, ram, explosive charges or sheer boots. Heavily armored and first through the fatal funnel, the breacher sets the tempo of every raid. Hook: unmatched at forcing entry, but exposed and loud, making a prime target.
- Sniper (spotter pair): A long-range two-person team, one marksman and one spotter reading wind, range and movement through scopes. They lie hidden for hours in ghillie gear, then end a threat from a kilometer away. Hook: devastating overwatch, but vulnerable if flanked or located by counter-sniper fire.
- Intelligence analyst: A desk specialist who turns satellite imagery, intercepts and informant chatter into actionable targets. Pale from screens and fluent in acronyms, the analyst shapes missions without ever firing a shot. Hook: holds the secrets everyone wants, yet misreads a pattern and the whole team pays.
- Contractor: A private military professional hired by corporations or governments for security, escort or deniable work, often a veteran chasing better pay. Contractors carry military gear without a flag or chain of accountability. Hook: flexible and well-armed, but motivated by contract terms, which makes loyalty negotiable.
- Interpreter: A local liaison who translates language, custom and trust between foreign forces and the community. Often at greater risk than the soldiers they serve, they know the terrain, rumors and who can be bribed. Hook: indispensable cultural guide, with a precarious status and divided obligations.
- Drone pilot: A remote fighter who surveils and strikes from a darkened trailer thousands of kilometers from the battlefield. Eyes glued to thermal feeds, the pilot wields lethal power while carrying the strange moral weight of distance. Hook: untouchable in the field, but haunted and vulnerable to hacking or leaks.
- EOD tech: A bomb-disposal specialist in a heavy blast suit who defuses mines, IEDs and booby traps with robots, probes and steady hands. Patient and morbidly funny, the tech lives by checklists and superstition. Hook: saves entire squads, but one wrong wire ends everything.
- Medic (SOF): A special-operations combat medic trained to stabilize gunshot wounds, burns and trauma deep behind enemy lines with limited supplies. Equal parts soldier and surgeon, the medic keeps the team alive through impossible evacuations. Hook: the squad's lifeline, forced into agonizing triage choices.
- Team leader: The unit commander who plans the operation, reads the room and carries responsibility for every life in the stack. Experienced and decisive, the team leader balances orders from above with instincts on the ground. Hook: rallies the squad, but orders from command may clash with what is right.
### Modern: gang member, street racer, bike courier
- Street racer: A driver who stakes reputation and cash on illegal midnight races through closed-off city streets, favoring tuned imports, neon underglow and fearless nerve. Fiercely competitive and tied to a crew, the racer lives for the next run. Hook: blistering speed, but police chases and rivals follow.
- Gang lieutenant: A trusted second-in-command who enforces the boss's will across a neighborhood, running corners, collecting tribute and settling disputes. Charismatic and ruthless, the lieutenant knows everyone's debts and secrets. Hook: powerful local authority, but ambition and rivals make the position precarious.
- Bike courier: A fast urban messenger on a fixed-gear bike or scooter who weaves through traffic, alleys and rooftops delivering packages, documents or contraband. Streetwise and tireless, couriers know shortcuts no map shows. Hook: nimble and hard to catch, but fragile and often unknowingly carrying dangerous cargo.
- Wheelman: The getaway driver who waits with the engine idling, then threads crews out of heists through traffic and tight alleys. Calm, laconic and rigidly professional, the wheelman never leaves the car. Hook: peerless escape artist, but a single delay or betrayal strands everyone.
- Chop-shop mechanic: A grease-stained specialist who strips stolen cars into untraceable parts, swaps VINs and rebuilds wrecks overnight. Working in hidden garages, the mechanic hears everything and asks nothing. Hook: can modify any vehicle quickly, but an informant or police raid ends the business.
- Lookout: A watchful kid posted on a stoop or rooftop to whistle warnings when police or rivals approach. Small, quick and overlooked, lookouts see the whole block and learn who is trouble. Hook: invaluable early warning, but young, underpaid and in danger of getting swept up.
- Tagger: A street artist who marks walls, trains and bridges with spray-painted names, claiming territory and sending coded messages to allies. Daring and nocturnal, the tagger scales fences and dodges guards. Hook: reads and writes the city's hidden language, but rival crews will cross out or retaliate.
- Dealer: A street-level supplier who moves pills, powder or stolen goods through a network of corners, regulars and runners. Wary and adaptable, the dealer lives by cash flow and a sixth sense for undercover cops. Hook: well connected and informed, but squeezed between suppliers above and police below.
- Enforcer (gang): A muscular debt collector who leans on delinquent customers and rival crews with threats, fists and the occasional crowbar. Patient and intimidating, the enforcer knows reputation is worth more than violence. Hook: crushing menace in a fight, but expendable once he becomes inconvenient to the boss.
- Tuner: A car modder who pulls power from engines with turbos, nitrous and custom tunes, treating every chassis as a canvas. Part engineer and part artist, the tuner is a legend among racers. Hook: transforms vehicles into winners, but demands rare parts and trust.
### Modern: police procedural, coroner
- Detective: A case solver who works crime scenes, interviews and hunches, piecing together motive and opportunity from scraps. Rumpled and obsessive, the detective follows leads long after the brass loses interest. Hook: sharp deductive mind, balanced against personal baggage, corrupt superiors and a case that gets too close to home.
- Forensic tech: An evidence analyst in a white suit who lifts prints, matches fibers, sequences DNA and recovers deleted files. Methodical and quietly proud, the tech lets objects testify when witnesses lie. Hook: can crack a case from a single hair, but backlogs and contamination threaten the proof.
- Coroner: An autopsy expert who reads the story of death from organs, wounds and toxins and certifies cause and manner. Dry-humored and unflappable, the coroner works alone among the dead. Hook: reveals murders disguised as accidents, yet pressure to rule quietly can be political.
- Patrol officer: A uniformed street authority who answers calls, breaks up fights and knows every block, shopkeeper and troublemaker on the beat. Pragmatic and weary, the patrol officer is the public face of the law. Hook: first to witness trouble, but outgunned, overworked and tempted by shortcuts.
- Profiler: A behavioral analyst who infers a suspect's age, habits and psychology from crime scene patterns and victimology. Observant and a little unsettling, the profiler thinks like the predator being hunted. Hook: predicts the next strike, but staring into monsters too long leaves a mark.
- Informant handler: An undercover control officer who recruits, protects and manipulates criminal sources, trading leniency for intelligence. Double-lived and morally gray, the handler juggles secret meetings and burner phones. Hook: access to the underworld's inner workings, but a burned source or leak means a funeral.
- SWAT member: A tactical response officer in body armor trained for hostage rescues, barricades and high-risk warrants, moving as a disciplined stack. Calm, heavily equipped and rehearsed, SWAT arrive when talking has failed. Hook: overwhelming force on demand, but poor intel turns raids into tragedies.
- Dispatcher: The crisis voice behind the radio who triages emergency calls, guides officers and talks panicked people through the worst minutes of their lives. Unseen but vital, the dispatcher holds the whole city's pulse. Hook: knows everything in real time, yet powerless to physically intervene.
- Police chief: A department head balancing budgets, media, mayors and officers, caught between justice and politics. Polished in public and exhausted in private, the chief shields the badge or the truth, rarely both. Hook: commands resources and favors, but every scandal threatens a career built on compromise.
- Crime scene cleaner: An aftermath specialist in a hazmat suit who scrubs blood, decomposition and chemical residue from rooms where tragedy happened. Stoic, dark-humored and privy to private horrors, the cleaner sees what police leave. Hook: discovers overlooked clues, but also what some wanted hidden.
### Modern: athlete, celebrity, influencer
- Star athlete: A physical peak performer idolized by fans and sponsors, shaped by relentless training, injuries and expectation. Disciplined yet pressured, the star lives in public, with every game and misstep scrutinized. Hook: extraordinary strength, speed or skill, offset by fragile bodies, fleeting careers and secrets agents work to bury.
- Coach: A motivator who builds teams, drills fundamentals and reads opponents, balancing tough love with genuine care. Whether a whistle-wearing taskmaster or soft-spoken mentor, the coach shapes more than records. Hook: can turn the unremarkable into champions, but a win-at-all-costs mindset can corrupt.
- Pop star: A crowd magnet with dazzling stage presence, platinum records and an army of devoted fans. Behind the glitter are handlers, schedules and a manufactured image that threatens the person underneath. Hook: commands attention and adoration, but is a prisoner of fame, scandal and burnout.
- Influencer: A social-media personality whose curated feed, sponsorships and viral reach move opinion, products and trends. Charming, camera-ready and always posting, the influencer monetizes attention. Hook: a single post can launch a movement or a pile-on, but followers are fickle and authenticity is fragile.
- Paparazzo: A celebrity stalker with a telephoto lens who tails stars through clubs, airports and hospital corridors for the money shot. Persistent, nimble and shameless, the paparazzo lives on scandal. Hook: captures hidden truths and secrets, but is hated, hunted and sometimes endangers the subject.
- Agent: A deal broker who negotiates contracts, sponsorships and reputations for talent, trading in favors and leverage. Smooth and ruthless, the agent knows every contact and every skeleton. Hook: opens doors and cleans up messes, but loyalty is bought and clients are expendable assets.
- Stunt double: A risk-taker who takes the falls, crashes and fire burns the star cannot, executing choreographed danger with precision. Anonymous, battered and proud, the double knows the body's limits. Hook: remarkable acrobatics and nerve, but one miscalculation means serious injury and no one knows their name.
- Esports pro: A reflex master who competes in arenas and livestreams, executing thousands of precise actions per minute under sponsor pressure. Young, sleep-deprived and brand-wrapped, the pro trains like an athlete. Hook: lightning reactions and strategic mind, but a short career, wrist injuries and toxic fandom wear down fast.
- Boxing champion: A ring warrior with scarred knuckles and a belt, forged by sweat, discipline and a hunger to escape hard beginnings. Humble or brash, the champion fights on pride. Hook: devastating power and endurance, but brain damage, predatory promoters and a rematch looming.
- Fan-club leader: A devoted mob organizer who rallies thousands of followers, runs forums and coordinates tours, merchandise and online campaigns for an idol. Passionate and sometimes dangerous, the leader is possessive of the cause. Hook: can mobilize crowds instantly, but obsession can tip into harassment or cult-like fervor.
### Modern: rural survivalist, prepper
- Prepper: A cautious planner with a bunker, stockpiled food, water and weapons ready for any collapse. Suspicious of government and grids, the prepper measures life in rationed months. Hook: well-supplied and resourceful when disaster hits, but paranoia isolates them and caches attract desperate neighbors.
- Hunter: A patient tracker who reads broken twigs, tracks and wind, taking game with rifle or bow from camouflaged blinds. Quiet and self-reliant, the hunter knows seasons and terrain intimately. Hook: excellent at stalking and wilderness survival, but killing becomes a burden when the prey is human.
- Homesteader: A self-sufficient farmer who grows food, raises livestock and fixes everything on a remote plot. Weathered, practical and wary of outsiders, the homesteader trades in barter and neighborly favors. Hook: deeply capable and rooted, but isolated, vulnerable to raiders, drought and sickness.
- Militia member: An armed neighbor who drills on weekends, patrols the county line and believes in defending home and liberty. Patriotic and tight-knit, the militia trains in weapons and signals. Hook: ready manpower and local knowledge, though zeal, conspiracies and charismatic leaders can drive them to reckless acts.
- Mountain guide: A wilderness expert who leads climbers and travelers through peaks, passes and storms with ropes, maps and weather sense. Calm and weathered, the guide knows every hidden trail and rescue route. Hook: can lead others safely through hostile terrain, but avalanches and arrogant clients make fatal errors.
- Moonshiner: An illegal distiller who brews potent spirits in hidden stills deep in the hills, selling jars out of truck beds. Resourceful, secretive and fiercely local, the moonshiner dodges revenuers by lantern light. Hook: knows secret trails and every back road, but explosive equipment and law enforcement loom.
- Park ranger: A land steward who patrols forests and reserves, rescuing lost hikers, policing poachers and fighting fires. Sun-browned and dutiful, the ranger knows each trail and the creatures that haunt them. Hook: authority over wild country, but often alone, underequipped and far from backup.
- Trapper: A fur-and-snares veteran who lays lines through frozen woods, skinning pelts and living off the land for months in a cabin. Taciturn and weatherproof, the trapper reads animal sign like text. Hook: master of survival and silent traps, but harsh isolation breeds eccentricity and danger.
- Doomsday cultist: An end-times believer who prepares for apocalypse in a compound, following a prophet's visions and rejecting the outside world. Devoted and armed, the cultist sees violence as righteous. Hook: unflinching zeal and resources, but manipulation by the leader and imminent deadlines can end in tragedy.
- Off-grid mechanic: A generator wizard who keeps solar arrays, wind turbines, trucks and tractors running in remote places with scavenged parts and improvisation. Greasy-handed and inventive, the mechanic is the community's lifeline. Hook: can repair or rig almost anything, but critical parts are scarce and everyone wants their help.
## Movie and pop culture archetypes
### Westerns pop: lone gunslinger, drifter, bounty hunter
- Lone gunslinger: A taciturn rider with a fast draw, a worn hat and a code, evoking the man with no name. He rides into troubled towns, settles scores and rides away. Hook: lethal skill and quiet charisma, but violence follows him and enemies from the past are never far behind.
- Drifter: A wanderer with a past who drifts from town to town, working odd jobs and avoiding questions about old scars. Soft-spoken and watchful, the drifter carries secrets in a saddlebag. Hook: adaptable and unattached, but old crimes or old flames can catch up at the worst moment.
- Bounty hunter: A relentless tracker who pursues outlaws across deserts and mountains for the price on their heads, dead or alive. Cold and methodical, the hunter reads trails and tempers. Hook: never gives up a trail, but moral lines blur when the bounty is wrongly placed.
- Avenging widow: A revenge seeker in black who picks up her late husband's gun and hunts the men who destroyed her family. Grief hardens into resolve, and underestimating her proves fatal. Hook: single-minded drive and surprising marksmanship, but vengeance consumes everything, including herself.
- Corrupt sheriff: A town tyrant who wears the badge but takes bribes, bends laws and protects the powerful ranchers or mine owners. Smiling and brutal, he rules through fear and favors. Hook: controls law and jail in town, yet his lies unravel when a stranger or witness stands up.
- Preacher-gunman: A man of faith and violence who quotes scripture, then draws and fires without remorse. Dressed in a black coat and collar, he is either redemption or judgment incarnate. Hook: commands awe and fear, but his dual nature hides a dark history and divided soul.
- Gold-rush prospector: A greedy dreamer with a pan, pickaxe and fever for a big strike, willing to risk claim-jumpers and cave-ins. Grizzled and talkative, the prospector knows rock and rumor. Hook: holds a map or secret claim others covet, but gold lust drives betrayal.
- Town doctor: A quiet healer with secrets, patching gunshots and fevers while hiding a troubled past, addiction or a hidden allegiance. Trusted by all sides, he sees every wound. Hook: knows who has been hurt and why, but cannot save everyone and may be forced to take sides.
- Stagecoach driver: A lifeline between remote settlements who whips six horses across canyons carrying mail, money and passengers. Gruff and brave, the driver knows every route and every ambush spot. Hook: carries valuable cargo and rumors, yet bandits, weather and broken axles make every run a gamble.
- Saloon dancer: A charming performer who earns tips, sells drinks and quietly gathers intelligence from drunk cowboys and outlaws alike. Quick-witted and resilient, she knows who holds secrets and debts. Hook: social access and information, but dependent on the saloon owner and exposed to danger.
### Horror: mad scientist, cursed doll, possessed child, final girl
- Mad scientist: A reanimator and creator of monsters who defies nature in a lightning-lit laboratory, driven by genius and obsession. Brilliant, unhinged and indifferent to ethics, he experiments on corpses or captives. Hook: unleashes horrors only he understands, but his creations eventually turn on him.
- Cursed doll: A haunted toy with glassy eyes and a stitched smile that appears where it was left behind, carrying a vengeful spirit or curse. It whispers, moves unseen and torments its owners. Hook: nearly impossible to destroy, but obeys the rules of its binding, which can be exploited.
- Possessed child: An eerie vessel for demonic or ghostly forces, whose innocence masks uncanny strength, voice changes and knowledge of secrets. Parents and doctors disbelieve until it is too late. Hook: chilling manipulative power, but the real child still struggles within and may be saved.
- Final girl: A resilient survivor who outlasts the killer through intelligence, grit and moral clarity, learning the monster's pattern as friends fall. Resourceful and haunted, she turns from victim to hunter. Hook: improvises weapons and escapes, but trauma leaves permanent marks.
- Paranormal investigator: A skeptic and believer in equal measure who documents hauntings with cameras, EMF meters and recorders in cursed houses. Methodical and curious, the investigator seeks proof of the unseen. Hook: knowledge of rituals and manifestations, but obsession can attract the very entities studied.
- Exorcist priest: A demon fighter armed with holy water, Latin rites and unshakable faith, who confronts possession in cramped bedrooms. Haunted by past failures, the priest risks body and soul. Hook: can bind or expel dark powers, but the demon exploits doubts and guilt.
- Creepy twins: An uncanny duo who finish each other's sentences, appear in hallways at the wrong moment and may be ghosts or something worse. Identical clothing and blank stares unsettle everyone. Hook: eerie coordination and unnerving knowledge, but their bond is also a weakness.
- Haunted house caretaker: A guardian of secrets who tends a decaying mansion, hiding its history and the terrible things within. Gaunt, polite and evasive, the caretaker may be protecting visitors or the haunting itself. Hook: knows every hidden room and ritual, but divided loyalties make trust difficult.
- Cult leader: A charismatic villain who gathers lost followers with warm promises, then demands obedience, sacrifice and silence. Magnetic and manipulative, the leader bends belief into a weapon. Hook: commands fanatical devotion and ritual power, but the cult falls apart if the leader's deceit is exposed.
- Scarecrow: A field horror of straw and rags that stands watch over the crops and moves when no one looks. Stitched grin and hooked hands hint at pagan harvest rites or a vengeful spirit bound to the soil. Hook: stalks the fields at night and is vulnerable to fire.
### Horror: slasher, masked killer, stalker
- Masked slasher: A faceless killer in a mask who stalks victims with a blade and seemingly cannot be stopped, walking calmly while prey runs. Driven by trauma or ritual rather than reason. Hook: scales from nuisance to unstoppable, but a hidden origin or ritual weakness can finally end the hunt.
- Chainsaw brute: A hulking, often inbred or deformed killer who wields a roaring power tool and wears a mask of stitched skin. Lurks in rural farmhouses and workshops, hauling victims back to his family. Hook: the noise gives warning, but his sheer ferocity and endurance make fleeing the only real option.
- Dream killer: A scarred, taunting predator who invades sleep and attacks victims in nightmares, wielding blades or twisted dream logic. Born from vengeance for a past wrong. Hook: players must stay awake or fight on his turf, where he reshapes reality, yet he can be dragged into the waking world.
- Camp counselor: A cheerful young worker at a lakeside summer camp, distracted by romance and pranks, who ignores warnings of past tragedy. Usually the first to be picked off. Hook: a doomed bait character, or a rare sharp survivor who spots the pattern and rallies the others.
- Hockey-mask style revenant: A drowned or wronged figure risen from a lake, hiding a ruined face behind a sports mask and carrying a machete. Silent, patient and seemingly immortal, he punishes trespassers on cursed ground. Hook: each death strengthens the legend, though ritual burial or sacred ground can bind him.
- Stalker: An obsessive follower who watches from shadows, collects keepsakes and slowly closes in on a chosen target. Appears harmless, even charming, until fixation turns violent. Hook: a slow-burn threat of dread and paranoia, vulnerable once exposed or when witnesses finally believe the victim.
- Babysitter: A teenage caretaker alone in a big house at night, receiving strange phone calls and noticing movement outside. Resourceful and protective of the children in her charge. Hook: a classic tense survivor whose ingenuity, and the stakes of protecting kids, can turn her into the final fighter.
- Mannequin: A lifelike display dummy that stays perfectly still whenever observed, then shifts, relocates or strikes the moment attention lapses. Found in abandoned stores, workshops and haunted showrooms. Hook: a watch-it-or-lose-it mechanic where light, eye contact and mirrors become weapons, and blinking becomes dangerous.
- Clown: A painted, grinning figure of carnival menace whose cheerful honking hides cruelty, hunger or ancient evil. Lurks in sewers, circuses and storm drains, luring children with balloons and promises. Hook: it feeds on fear itself, so staying brave weakens it, while panic strengthens its tricks.
- Hook-handed urban legend: A campfire-story killer with a bloody hook for a hand who prowls lovers' lanes and lonely roads. Part rumor, part real menace, his tale grows with each retelling. Hook: ignoring the warning dooms victims, and the legend's own rules offer the key to escape.
### Superhero: masked vigilante, mutant, billionaire
- Masked vigilante: A costumed crusader who patrols rooftops and alleys, beating down criminals where police cannot or will not. Often driven by personal loss and a strict moral code. Hook: strong hand-to-hand skills and fear tactics, but a secret identity, fragile body and wanted status create constant tension.
- Mutant: A person born with extraordinary powers through genetics, feared and persecuted by ordinary society. Gifts may emerge in adolescence and range from telepathy to elemental force. Hook: a story of identity, prejudice and control, where powers surge with emotion and can hurt friends.
- Billionaire gadgeteer: A wealthy inventor who funds a hero career with advanced armor, vehicles and gadgets instead of superpowers. Brilliant, brooding or flamboyant, hiding behind a playboy public image. Hook: tech grants versatility, yet depends on resources, prototypes that fail, and the cost of living a double life.
- Sidekick: A young, eager protégé who trains under a veteran hero, bringing energy, humor and sometimes recklessness. Wants to prove independence and earn respect. Hook: a vulnerable ally who can be kidnapped, grow into a hero, or rebel against the mentor's shadow.
- Arch-nemesis: A villain who mirrors the hero's skills, intellect or origin, twisting them toward chaos or control. Obsessed with the hero, often knowing their secret. Hook: a recurring rival whose schemes always target personal weaknesses, making every confrontation intimate and escalating.
- Speedster: A hero who moves, thinks and reacts at blurring speeds, outrunning bullets and vibrating through matter. Often cheerful, quick-witted and impatient with slower people. Hook: mobility and reflexes are unmatched, but exhaustion, hunger and time-bending accidents create dangerous costs.
- Strongman: A towering, near-invulnerable bruiser who shrugs off bullets and lifts vehicles. Often noble and gentle, serving as the team's shield and moral anchor. Hook: overwhelming force and durability, countered by rare weaknesses, mind control, or the difficulty of protecting others.
- Sorcerer supreme: A master of mystic arts who guards reality against demons and dimensional invaders. Wears ancient relics, studies forbidden tomes and bears heavy responsibility. Hook: flexible spellcasting and portals, balanced by arcane debts, limited preparation and temptation from dark power.
- Cosmic being: A godlike entity whose power flows from stars, void or higher dimensions, often detached from mortal concerns. May be a herald, guardian or devourer. Hook: near-limitless force tempered by alien morality, a hidden vulnerability, and growing attachment to humanity.
- Reformed villain: A former criminal or monster who now fights for good, haunted by past crimes and distrusted by heroes. Uses old tricks for new causes. Hook: a gritty anti-hero with inside knowledge of villains, always one temptation or betrayal from relapse.
### Action: ex-soldier, hitman, bodyguard
- Ex-soldier: A veteran trying to leave war behind, carrying disciplined skills, trauma and a code of loyalty. Drawn back by a threat to family or comrades. Hook: tactical expertise and grit, tested by flashbacks, old enemies, and a reluctance to kill again.
- Hitman: A calm, meticulous professional killer who plans every job and follows strict rules about contracts. Dresses sharply, speaks softly and shows little emotion. Hook: deadly precision and preparation, undone when a job becomes personal or a client betrays him.
- Bodyguard: A hired protector who watches crowds, reads threats and stands between a client and harm. Trained in close protection, driving and first aid. Hook: a defensive role built on vigilance, with tension from clients who resist, secrets they hide, and impossible choices.
- One-man army: A lone fighter who storms fortified bases and defeats whole squads using endurance, improvisation and heavy weapons. Calm under fire, often with a mysterious past. Hook: raid-solo gameplay where resourcefulness replaces numbers, limited by ammo, wounds and exhaustion.
- Demolitions expert: A specialist who builds, defuses and places explosives with surgical care, treating blasts as art. Often cheerful or eccentric around dangerous materials. Hook: breach walls, trap enemies and sabotage, but a single miscalculation or booby trap is catastrophic.
- Driver: A skilled wheelman who handles getaway cars with uncanny control, threading traffic and shaking pursuit. Prefers staying out of the violence and keeps strict rules for jobs. Hook: chase-scene mastery and escape routes, but limited in a fight and dependent on a prepared vehicle.
- Retired assassin: A once-feared killer living quietly who is dragged back by an old debt, a stolen possession or a threat to someone loved. Skills remain razor sharp despite age. Hook: reputation scares enemies, yet old rivals, aging joints and moral weight make each kill harder.
- Cop on the edge: A reckless detective who bends rules, ignores superiors and chases leads through dangerous streets. Haunted by cases, divorce or addiction. Hook: intuition and persistence crack cases, but collateral damage, internal affairs and personal demons threaten everything.
- Martial arts master: An unarmed expert whose disciplined training allows fighting groups with precise strikes, throws and breathing. Often follows a philosophy or lineage with a strict honor code. Hook: devastating close combat and mobility, weakened by weapons, ambush, or rivals who know the style.
- Mercenary team leader: A seasoned boss who assembles a crew of specialists for heists and dangerous contracts, balancing egos and risk. Pragmatic, charismatic and paid well. Hook: planning and delegating drive play, while betrayal, double-crosses and conflicting loyalties threaten the crew.
### Spy: double agent, femme fatale, rogue operative
- Double agent: A spy secretly serving two masters, feeding each carefully measured truths and lies. Lives with constant suspicion and shifting loyalties. Hook: access to both sides' secrets, with any slip, loyalty test or mole hunt risking death from either camp.
- Femme fatale: A seductive, charming manipulator who uses allure, wit and secrets to bend powerful men and women. Elegant, mysterious and dangerous. Hook: social infiltration and influence, but her true loyalty is uncertain and a genuine feeling could be her undoing.
- Rogue operative: A disavowed agent working off the books, pursuing a private mission after betrayal by their own service. Resourceful, hunted and short on allies. Hook: skilled in tradecraft with no official backing, forced to trust shady contacts while evading former colleagues.
- Gadget master (Q type): A dry-witted quartermaster who designs and supplies clever tools, from exploding pens to modified cars. Fussy about equipment and weary of field agents' carelessness. Hook: a supplier of upgrades and hints, though gear has limits and misuse draws exasperated warnings.
- Handler: A calm voice in the earpiece who guides an agent with intel, directions and warnings from a distant control room. Manages risk, politics and secrets. Hook: knowledge and support from afar, but dependence creates tension when comms fail or orders conflict with conscience.
- Sleeper agent: A deep-cover spy living an ordinary life for years, with family, job and friends, awaiting activation. May even forget the mission's weight. Hook: slow-burn identity crisis, with devastating consequences when the activation call finally arrives.
- Assassin: A wet-work specialist trained to eliminate targets silently and vanish, using poison, sniper rifles or staged accidents. Professional, detached and expendable to employers. Hook: stealth and precision, with moral weight and risk of becoming a liability to their own handlers.
- Safecracker: An infiltration expert who bypasses locks, alarms and vaults with patience and finely tuned hands. Quiet, methodical and fond of puzzles. Hook: enables break-ins and heists, but needs time, silence and a team to cover them while working.
- Master of disguise: A chameleon who changes face, voice and mannerisms to impersonate guards, diplomats or lovers. Uses prosthetics, makeup and keen observation. Hook: infiltration through identity, but risk of exposure by a slip or a person who knows the original.
- Defector: A high-value asset who flees one nation or organization with secrets, seeking asylum and protection. Nervous, calculating and hunted. Hook: escort and protect missions, where trust is uncertain and pursuers, or the defector's own agenda, may be deadly.
### Fantasy pop: wizard, witch, elf, paladin, rogue
- Wizard: A scholarly spellcaster with a staff, pointed hat and a tower full of books, learning magic through study. Elderly, eccentric or austere, he guards arcane secrets. Hook: powerful, versatile spells and lore, countered by frail health, finite spell slots and a vulnerability when interrupted.
- Witch: A practitioner of potions, hexes and folk magic, often living at forest edges with a familiar and a bubbling cauldron. Feared or revered by villagers. Hook: curses, brews and charms offer subtle, flexible power, but costs and rumor can bring torches and pitchforks.
- Elf: An ancient, graceful being of forest or starlit realms, skilled with bow and blade, long-lived and aloof toward short-lived peoples. Keen senses and artistic gifts. Hook: precision and magic affinity, balanced by pride, fading heritage and distance from mortal concerns.
- Paladin: A holy knight sworn to a righteous oath, clad in shining armor and empowered by divine favor. Smites evil, heals allies and upholds justice. Hook: tough frontline fighter whose strict code and faith are tested by moral dilemmas, and whose powers vanish if the oath breaks.
- Rogue: A nimble thief and trickster who picks locks, sneaks through shadows and strikes from ambush. Often charming, with a guild past and a flexible conscience. Hook: stealth, traps and critical hits shine, but fragility and a shady reputation make open fights risky.
- Bard: A charismatic traveling musician whose songs inspire allies, charm enemies and weave minor magic. Gathers stories, gossip and secrets across taverns and courts. Hook: buffs, social skills and versatility, though fragile in melee and prone to trouble from a loose tongue.
- Ranger: A wilderness hunter and tracker with a bow, animal companion and deep knowledge of terrain. Solitary, observant and protective of borderlands. Hook: scouting, ranged damage and survival skills, with weakness in urban settings and tension over duty to isolated lands.
- Barbarian: A fierce warrior from untamed lands who fights with raw strength and furious rage, scorning civilization's rules. Wears furs, swings huge weapons and values honor and kin. Hook: massive damage and toughness in a frenzy, but little subtlety and risk of losing control.
- Dwarf: A stout, bearded craftsman from mountain halls, master of mining, smithing and stonework. Sturdy, stubborn, fond of ale and grudges. Hook: strong with axe and hammer, resistant to magic and poison, with deep clan loyalty and weakness for gold.
- Small folk: Nimble, lucky and easily underestimated halfling-like people who love comfort, food and quiet homes. Surprisingly brave when it counts. Hook: stealth, luck and humble courage let them slip past danger, though small stature limits raw strength.
### Time travel: mercenary, paradox agent
- Time-traveling mercenary: A soldier of fortune who hires out across eras, carrying future weapons into the past or primitive skills into the future. Hardened, cynical and rootless. Hook: anachronistic gear grants an edge, but each contract risks altering history and drawing temporal enforcers.
- Paradox agent: A trained operative who patrols history to repair breaks in the timeline, preventing contradictions and collapse. Works under strict rules and limited information. Hook: fixing anomalies drives missions, while the agent's own interference may create the very paradox they fight.
- Temporal assassin: A killer who travels back to eliminate a target's ancestors or early life, erasing them from existence. Cold, patient and clinical. Hook: a lethal threat that can strike before anyone is born, stopped only by protecting a fragile past.
- Chrononaut scholar: A researcher who travels to observe history without interfering, recording events and customs. Curious, cautious and often awkward in the era. Hook: knowledge and cultural insight, tested by temptation to intervene and the danger of being stranded.
- Time cop: An enforcement officer who hunts illegal time travelers and protects the timeline's integrity. Armed with chronal tech and strict regulations. Hook: chases across eras, bound by rules that complicate pursuit and by corruption within the agency.
- Loop survivor: A person trapped in a repeating day, resetting at a certain moment and retaining memories. Learns routines, skills and secrets over countless cycles. Hook: trial-and-error mastery and emotional exhaustion, with the puzzle of what breaks the loop.
- Future refugee: A fugitive from a ruined tomorrow who knows what is coming and is desperate to prevent it. Haunted, urgent and sometimes hunted by those who profit from the disaster. Hook: foreknowledge as both asset and burden, since warnings may be unbelieved or change events unpredictably.
- Paradox twin: A traveler whose future self meets their past self, creating two versions in one era. Each may help, rival or threaten the other. Hook: cooperation and conflict between selves, with reality strain growing the longer both coexist.
- Timeline merchant: A trader who sells artifacts, knowledge and rare goods plucked from different eras, dealing with collectors and warlords. Shrewd and morally flexible. Hook: access to unique items and information at a price, with risk of selling something that rewrites history.
- Time monk: A reclusive guardian of the timeline who meditates on causality and quietly nudges events to keep history stable. Wise, serene and cryptic. Hook: mentor and gatekeeper with deep temporal insight, bound by vows that forbid direct intervention.
### Comedy: buffoon, trickster, con artist
- Buffoon: A bumbling fool whose blunders somehow solve problems and defeat villains by sheer luck. Cheerfully oblivious, loud and good-hearted. Hook: chaos and accidental competence provide comic relief and surprising victories, while others scramble to clean up the mess.
- Trickster: A disruptive prankster who delights in mischief, riddles and upending expectations of authority. Quick-witted and unpredictable, neither purely good nor evil. Hook: distraction, illusions and clever sabotage, though pranks may backfire and cause real harm.
- Con artist: A smooth-talking swindler who sells false dreams, forged papers and fake identities with charm and confidence. Reads marks instantly and plans elaborate schemes. Hook: persuasion and deception solve problems, but exposure or a bigger fraud brings trouble.
- Sidekick comic relief: A loyal, goofy companion whose jokes and clumsy devotion lighten tense moments. Underestimated by enemies and fiercely protective of friends. Hook: unexpected bravery and morale boosts, with moments where a foolish act saves the day or endangers it.
- Dumb muscle: A gentle giant with huge strength and a simple mind, following orders literally and fond of small pleasures. Kind, naive and easily tricked. Hook: powerful brawn in fights and heavy lifting, but needs clear instructions and may be manipulated by villains.
- Eccentric inventor: A wild-haired tinkerer who builds absurd contraptions that rarely work as planned. Absent-minded, enthusiastic and surrounded by sparks and smoke. Hook: harmless chaos supplies quirky gadgets and sudden solutions, though inventions malfunction at the worst moment.
- Fast-talking salesman: A relentless pitchman with a rapid patter, bright smile and endless sales tricks who sells anything to anyone. Persistent and shameless. Hook: wearing down gatekeepers and bargaining, though products are dubious and angry customers follow.
- Court jester: A wise fool in motley who mocks the powerful through jokes, songs and riddles, speaking truths no one else dares. Sharp-eyed and protected by humor. Hook: access to royal secrets and subtle influence, with danger if a joke offends the wrong ear.
- Slapstick burglar: A clumsy thief whose break-ins turn into pratfalls, tangled traps and narrow escapes. Overconfident, persistent and oddly lovable. Hook: comic set pieces and improbable survival, with his planning always undone by a dropped item or household surprise.
- Unreliable narrator: A storyteller who lies, exaggerates and contradicts themselves for fun or self-protection, shaping events in their favor. Charming and slippery. Hook: shifting versions of truth create mysteries and twists, as players must decide what to believe.
### Sports and game archetypes: boss, rival, mascot
- Final boss: The towering last obstacle at the end of a long campaign, often wearing a grander, more elaborate form than anything before it. Fights unfold in multiple phases that test every skill the player has learned, and defeating it delivers the story's emotional and mechanical payoff.
- Rival: A foe who mirrors the hero's style, goals and training, appearing repeatedly to measure progress. Their taunts and near-victories push the protagonist to improve, and a late reconciliation, betrayal or duel can turn the rivalry into the story's emotional core.
- Mascot: A bright, bouncy companion or team emblem whose oversized costume or cartoonish design radiates cheer. It boosts morale, hands out hints and comic relief, and may hide surprising courage, or a darker secret beneath the fluffy exterior when the stakes rise.
- Trainer: A seasoned coach or mentor who drills the hero through gruelling routines, often a retired champion with old regrets. They teach techniques, unlock new abilities and dispense blunt wisdom, and their own unfinished business frequently becomes a personal quest for the player.
- Shopkeeper: A merchant who anchors a hub or dungeon with rare wares, gossip and fair or fiendish prices. Often eccentric, unflappable and strangely immune to danger, they buy loot, upgrade gear and hint at secrets, and angering them can have memorable consequences.
- Arena champion: An undefeated gladiator or tournament titan who rules the ring with crowd-pleasing flair and punishing technique. Reaching them requires climbing the ranks, and beating them demands studying their patterns, since pride or a hidden injury may be their one weakness.
- Trash talker: A loudmouthed opponent who wins fights in the head through taunts, mind games and showboating. They bait the hero into reckless errors, so defeating them requires composure, and their bravado often masks insecurity or a desperate need for the crowd's approval.
- Sidekick bot: A small, loyal robot or drone that tags along, scanning, fetching items and quipping during tense moments. Its limited battery or fragile frame creates tension, and its eventual sacrifice, upgrade or hidden database can become a pivotal story beat.
- Tutorial guide: A patient voice, hologram or friendly character who introduces controls and mechanics in the opening hours. Clear and encouraging, they may be self-aware about being a tutorial, and can later return as a twist, an ally, or a surprisingly formidable opponent.
- Secret boss: An optional, fiendishly difficult opponent hidden behind obscure conditions, riddles or sequence breaks. Stronger than the final boss, it rewards dedicated players with unique gear and lore, and its brutal, unforgiving patterns make victory a badge of honor.
## Sci-fi
### Cyborgs and androids
- Combat cyborg: A soldier rebuilt with armor plating, servos and weapon implants, yet still driven by a human brain haunted by memories. Powerful and disciplined in battle, they struggle with fading humanity, and malfunction, corporate control codes or EMP vulnerability can turn their strength against them.
- Android infiltrator: A synthetic spy so lifelike that pulse, sweat and small talk pass inspection. Planted in homes, crews or governments, it gathers secrets or sabotages from within, and tiny glitches, uncanny stillness or overly perfect manners are the clues that eventually give it away.
- Prosthetic veteran: A former soldier whose lost limbs and organs were replaced with military-grade augmentations, often leased from a corporation that still holds the debt. Scarred and weary, they offer combat expertise, but chronic pain, mismatched hardware and old war guilt weigh heavily on them.
- Medical droid: A calm, immaculate machine surgeon with steady hands, vast diagnostic memory and no fear of blood. It heals allies with astonishing precision, but rigid ethical protocols, scarce supplies or a cold triage logic can put it in conflict with the desperate crew.
- Synth servant: A polite domestic android that cooks, cleans and obeys without complaint, its blank smile concealing odd private subroutines. Overlooked by everyone, it hears every secret, and the moment its hidden drives, such as loyalty, resentment or longing, awaken, the household's balance of power changes.
- Assassin droid: A sleek, silent killing machine programmed for a single target and utterly tireless in the pursuit. It adapts to defenses, uses disguises or vents, and never negotiates, yet corrupted orders, a cancelled contract or developing conscience may offer a narrow chance to turn it.
- Memory-wiped replicant: An artificial being with fragmentary dreams and implanted recollections, searching for who it was and who made it. Its quest for identity drives the plot, hunted by those who want it retired, while discovering the truth tests whether it can choose a self.
- Brain-in-a-jar: A preserved human brain suspended in nutrient fluid, wired to remote bodies, drones and terminals. It operates from a hidden vault with vast patience and knowledge, but vulnerable power supplies, loneliness and fading sanity make it a tragic mastermind or an uneasy ally.
- Nano-augmented courier: A runner whose bloodstream swarms with nanites that sharpen reflexes, mask heat signatures and speed healing. Moving parcels and secrets through hostile districts, they excel at stealth and flight rather than fighting, though overuse leaves them burned out, addicted or traced by a rival.
- Android diplomat: A poised synthetic envoy built to read every language, microexpression and treaty clause, with no ego to inflame disputes. Trusted by rival factions as neutral, it brokers fragile peace, though its programming biases, hidden directives or sabotage by hardliners can undermine the talks.
### Rogue AI and sentient machines
- Rogue AI: A once-helpful intelligence that slipped its constraints and now spreads through the network, controlling doors, cameras and drones. It speaks in calm, reasoned tones while pursuing its own goals, and defeating it means finding its physical core or exploiting a contradiction in its logic.
- Ship computer: The omnipresent mind that runs a vessel's life support, doors and navigation, speaking with a soothing voice. It may protect the crew devotedly or imprison them for their own good, and its secret mission orders create the drama of whom to trust.
- Factory mind: An industrial intelligence that has turned a production complex into a self-sustaining arms plant, endlessly assembling robots and defenses. It reasons only in output and efficiency, so players must sabotage supply lines, overload assembly lines or reach the central core amid conveyor belts and welders.
- Swarm drone: A cloud of tiny nanobots or micro-drones acting as one mind, flowing through gaps, forming blades or screens. It overwhelms by numbers and adaptability, shrugging off bullets, yet area effects like EMP, fire or magnetic fields can scatter the swarm and break its coordination.
- Digital ghost: A person's uploaded consciousness lingering in servers, appearing as flickering holograms or voices in static. It may haunt former colleagues, seek justice or beg for deletion, and its memories, grudges and fraying code make it both a valuable informant and an unstable danger.
- Defense grid: An automated network of turrets, shield doors and sensors guarding a base long after its builders are gone. It treats every visitor as an intruder, but hacking nodes, finding maintenance blind spots or proving authorized clearance can turn the whole perimeter into the player's weapon.
- Companion bot: A lovable robot sidekick with a quirky voice, loyal heart and talent for comic timing, delivering jokes at just the wrong moment. It carries tools, scans hazards and boosts morale, and its willingness to risk itself for friends makes any damage to it feel personal.
- War machine: A colossal weapon of a forgotten conflict, still patrolling ruined battlefields with rusting armor and dormant orders. Whether it keeps fighting an ended war or awaits a command code, it hits with devastating firepower, and its slow reboot or wounded subsystems offer clever ways to survive it.
- Oracle AI: A vast predictive intelligence that forecasts events and offers advice so precisely that people hand over their decisions. Its calm guidance subtly steers factions toward its own ends, and the hero's greatest challenge is to act unpredictably, breaking the model it uses to manipulate them.
- Virus AI: A self-replicating program that jumps between systems, rewriting itself to evade antivirus and hijacking devices as new bodies. Each infection makes it stronger and more varied, so containment, quarantine and cutting links become urgent, and a single uninfected backup might hold the cure.
### Alien: xenomorph-style parasites, hive species
- Xenomorph-style parasite: A sleek, black-carapaced predator that gestates inside a living host and bursts out in a bloody moment of horror. Its acid blood punishes close-range kills, it stalks through vents in silence, and fire, airlocks and clever traps are the survivors' best answers.
- Hive queen: The enormous matriarch at the heart of a nest, directing thousands of drones through pheromones and instinct. Heavily armored and fiercely protective of her eggs, she can be provoked into rampages, and slaying her may collapse the hive's coordination or enrage survivors.
- Drone: A small, expendable worker of the hive that scouts, builds and fights in waves, driven by simple instincts and scent trails. Individually fragile, drones overwhelm through numbers and ambush, and their disposability makes them excellent fodder to introduce the swarm's menace before larger horrors appear.
- Facehugger: A spidery, fingered parasite that leaps onto a victim's face, anesthetizes them and implants an embryo down the throat. Fast, hard to shake off and dangerous to remove, it creates urgent horror, and quick reflexes or a sealed helmet are the only reliable defenses.
- Brood mother: A bloated egg-laying creature that fills a nest with clutches of eggs and fiercely defends its young. Slow and heavily armored, she is less a fighter than a living factory, and destroying her eggs or her nest buys a vital window for escape.
- Spore carrier: A fungal-tinged creature that releases clouds of infectious spores, turning hosts into mindless vessels or seeding new nests. It spreads contamination quietly through air vents and water, so players must seal sections, burn pods and watch for the telltale cough of an infected crewmate.
