- lost prince (JRPG party): A noble youth hiding his birthright, raised in obscurity after his kingdom's fall or a coup. He carries a legendary blade, a royal sigil or a haunted legacy. His hook is reclaiming his throne, and his weakness is the burden of expectation and doubt.
- soldier (FPS classes): A versatile frontline infantryman with a reliable rifle, rocket launcher or grenades, and the skill to hold the middle of any firefight. He is the all-rounder everyone understands. His strength is flexibility, and his weakness is that he excels at nothing in particular.
- sniper (FPS classes): A patient long-range marksman who perches on rooftops with a scoped rifle, picking off targets with single lethal shots. Cold, silent and precise, he rules sightlines. His weakness is vulnerability at close quarters and the glint of his scope giving away his hiding spot.
- engineer (FPS classes): A tinkering builder who deploys turrets, repair stations and teleporters to lock down territory. Clever, practical and often bespectacled, he wins through preparation rather than aim. His weakness is exposure while building and structures that crumble to a good flanker.
- medic (FPS classes): A support specialist with a healing beam, syringe gun or med-kit who keeps the squad on its feet. Calm under fire and fiercely protective, he trades kills for lives. His hook is team sustain, and his weakness is being a priority target with little offense.
- scout (FPS classes): A lightning-fast skirmisher who zips around the map to flank, capture objectives and harass the enemy. Cocky, twitchy and bursting with energy, he dodges more than he trades hits. His weakness is fragility, since a single stray shotgun blast can end him.
- demolition (FPS classes): A grinning explosives expert who lobs grenades, plants charges and sticks mines to every doorway. Gleeful and reckless, he reshapes the battlefield with fire and rubble. His weakness is friendly fire and a lack of precision when the enemy slips past the blast radius.
- tank (MOBA roles): A bulwark champion with huge health and crowd-control abilities who dives in first to absorb damage and break enemy formations. Stoic and stubborn, he protects fragile allies. His hook is soaking pressure, and his weakness is low damage and being kited by ranged foes.
- support (MOBA roles): A utility-focused hero who heals, shields, wards and rescues allies, often sacrificing gold and glory for the team's victory. Selfless, observant and quietly decisive, she sees the map. Her weakness is fragility and dependence on carries who must convert her setup into kills.
- assassin (MOBA roles): A stealthy burst-damage killer who strikes from the shadows, deletes a vulnerable target in seconds and escapes before retaliation. Cunning and arrogant, he thrives on snowballing. His weakness is flimsy defenses and a need for perfect timing, since one mistake means death.
- mage (MOBA roles): A glass-cannon spellcaster who rains area damage and crowd control from behind the front line. Intellectual and menacing, she scales with levels and items. Her weakness is a short range and mana dependence, leaving her helpless once gap-closers reach her.
- marksman (MOBA roles): A ranged damage carry who starts weak but, with items and farm, shreds towers and champions with rapid attacks. Disciplined and patient, he must be defended early. His hook is late-game dominance, and his weakness is positioning, as an assassin reaching him ends the fight.
- jungler (MOBA roles): A roaming lone wolf who clears neutral monsters in the wilds between lanes, then ambushes enemy laners to swing momentum. Resourceful and unpredictable, he reads the map like a hunter. His weakness is vulnerability to invades and slow early pacing without a good camp route.
- scientist (Survival-horror): A haunted researcher who unleashed the outbreak or discovered its horrific cure, now racing to document, flee or atone. Brilliant and guilt-ridden, he holds the key to the plot in notes and keycards. His weakness is physical frailty and a moral compromise that comes back to bite.
- rookie cop (Survival-horror): A young, underprepared officer thrust into a nightmare on the first day of the job, armed with a pistol and scarce ammo. Brave and green, he learns survival the hard way in dark corridors. His hook is the growth from frightened novice to resolute survivor.
- hunter (Survival-horror): A seasoned monster killer, soldier or tracker with weapons, traps and a grim sense of humor, who treats the horror as just another job. Gruff and capable, he guides or protects the weaker survivors. His weakness is old trauma and recklessness when the creature looks familiar.
- doomed researcher (Survival-horror): A frantic scholar glimpsed only through recovered journals, voice recordings and bloody notes, slowly realizing what he has awakened. His fate is sealed before the player arrives, yet his warnings, codes and failed plans become vital clues. His hook is tragedy told through scattered documents.
- wanderer (Roguelike): A nameless adventurer who descends into a procedurally generated dungeon again and again, dying, learning and returning. Resourceful and expendable, she builds a different character each run from random finds. Her hook is mastery through failure, and her weakness is permadeath.
- relic merchant (Roguelike): A shrewd peddler lurking between floors who sells cursed trinkets, rare potions and reality-bending relics at steep prices. Sly and amused, he trades in gold, blood or memories. His hook is a tempting power spike with a hidden cost, and he is rarely trustworthy.
- shrine keeper (Roguelike): A robed, enigmatic caretaker of an altar who offers blessings, curses and gambles in return for sacrifices. Calm and cryptic, she weighs the wanderer's choices without judgment. Her hook is risk and reward, since a bold offering might grant glory or doom the run.
- vault guardian (Roguelike): A monstrous sentinel, such as a stone golem, undead knight or mechanical hound, who guards the treasure chamber at a floor's end. Imposing and relentless, it tests the build the player has assembled. Its hook is a punishing pattern fight, and it drops a prize worth the risk.
- shadow agent (Stealth): A silent infiltrator in dark clothing who slips past patrols, hacks terminals and eliminates targets without leaving a trace. Disciplined, resourceful and nearly invisible, she works with gadgets and patience. Her weakness is a limited arsenal and the cost of being spotted.
- patrolling guard (Stealth): A bored sentry walking a predictable route with a flashlight and a radio, easy to avoid until he notices a stray footprint or an open door. Not evil, just doing a job. His hook is a rhythm players study and exploit, and his weakness is inattention.
- informant (Stealth): A nervous contact who trades secrets, passwords and guard schedules for money or protection, often meeting in alleys and back rooms. Twitchy and self-serving, he knows too much. His hook is crucial intelligence, and his weakness is a loose tongue that might betray the agent.
- sleeping boss (Stealth): A powerful target dozing in a lavish chamber, guarded by locks, alarms and thick walls, who may be quietly assassinated or avoided entirely. Arrogant and complacent, he trusts his security. His hook is a tense choice between a silent kill and a loud, doomed brawl.
- mayor (City-builder): The ambitious steward of a growing town who sets zones, taxes and policy while balancing happy citizens against a thin budget. Political and pragmatic, the mayor is the player's avatar in spirit. The hook is difficult tradeoffs, and a single bad decision could bankrupt the city or spark a riot.
- builder (City-builder): A hardworking foreman or architect whose crews raise roads, houses and monuments across the map. Practical and proud, he turns blueprints into skylines. His hook is the quiet satisfaction of growth, and his weakness is overextension, since expansion outpaces resources and supplies.
- tax collector (City-builder): A stern, ink-stained official who knocks on every door to gather the funds that keep services running. Disliked yet necessary, he tracks every coin. His hook is the economy's lifeblood, and his weakness is the resentment of citizens who riot, hide wealth or flee.
- saboteur (City-builder): A hidden agent of a rival power, criminal syndicate or angry mob who sets fires, poisons wells and sparks unrest to wreck the metropolis. Cunning and patient, he exploits neglect and weak security. His hook is chaos from within, and the city must find him.
### Board game and card game characters
- king (Chess pieces): The weak but vital monarch of the board, who shuffles one square at a time and whose capture ends the game. Revered and cloistered, he is protected by every other piece. His hook is the entire contest revolving around his safety, and his weakness is his own fragility.
- queen (Chess pieces): The most powerful piece on the board, gliding any distance in any direction with ruthless grace. Regal and deadly, she dominates open ground and bears the army's offensive weight. Her hook is overwhelming mobility, and her weakness is that losing her early can cripple the whole strategy.
- bishop (Chess pieces): A diagonal-walking cleric who slips across the board on a single color, unseen until he strikes. Pious, scheming and sly, he works from the flanks. His hook is long-range precision, and his weakness is that he cannot cross to the opposite color without help.
- knight (Chess pieces): A horseman who leaps in an L-shaped path over other pieces, ignoring walls and blockades. Chivalrous yet unpredictable, he excels in crowded positions and delivers surprise forks. His weakness is short range, since open boards reduce his advantage.
- rook (Chess pieces): A stalwart tower or castle that charges straight along ranks and files with crushing force. Immovable and loyal, he guards the corners and the king's flank. His hook is open-line power in the endgame, and his weakness is clumsiness when the board is crowded.
- pawn (Chess pieces): A humble foot soldier who inches forward one step at a time, captures only diagonally and dreams of promotion on the far side. Expendable and numerous, pawns form the front lines. Their hook is the underdog arc, since one that survives may become a queen.
- jack (Tarot, playing-card court): A youthful page or knave of the court, quick, cunning and sometimes roguish, who runs errands for the royals. He is the lowest of the face cards but often the most mischievous. His hook is a trickster's role, and he can swing a game unexpectedly.
- queen (Tarot, playing-card court): A poised, commanding court lady, often depicted with a flower or scepter, who embodies wisdom, intuition or cunning. She rules her suit with elegant authority. Her hook is the power behind the throne, and her mood in a reading can mean nurture or manipulation.
- king (Tarot, playing-card court): A stern, bearded monarch of a suit who holds the final word in his domain. He represents mastery, authority and the weight of command. His hook is leadership, and his weakness is that rigid pride or tyranny can turn the same card into a warning.
- joker (Tarot, playing-card court): A grinning wildcard in motley who belongs to no suit and breaks every rule. Chaotic, clever and unpredictable, he can serve as a trump or a curse depending on the game. His hook is wild luck, and he often mocks the very kings he plays beside.
- Game-show host: A flashy, toothy emcee in a sparkling suit who runs outrageous contests with booming laughter, glittering prizes and razor-sharp patter. Behind the grin may lurk cruelty or desperation, as the show demands drama. His hook is turning contestants' dreams into entertainment, sometimes lethal.
- dealer: A poised, unflappable figure behind the green felt who shuffles, deals and controls the table's rhythm without ever betraying emotion. Fair on the surface, he reads every player's tells. His hook is knowing the cards, and his weakness is temptation, since favors from gamblers can corrupt him.
- Card sharp: Cunning gambler who cheats with deft hands and hidden aces, charming rich marks with easy smiles and clever patter. Dressed in sleeves heavy with secrets, she wins through misdirection rather than luck. Her hook is a daring con, and her weakness is a rival who spots the trick.
- Dice goblin: Gleeful, chaotic gremlin who lives for rolling bones and luck, hoarding polyhedral dice in a clinking sack. He cackles at critical hits, wails at fumbles and believes the dice speak. His hook is wild randomness that swings fortunes, and his weakness is superstition and sore-loser tantrums.
- Dungeon master: Storyteller who runs the world and controls every monster, sitting behind a screen to narrate wonders and horrors alike. Part referee, part author, the figure weaves plots, voices villains and rewards imagination. The hook is limitless creativity, and the weakness is the temptation to railroad, or to kill players out of spite.
- Mimic chest: Treasure box that sprouts teeth and ambushes looters, appearing as an innocent gold-banded chest that gnashes with a long tongue when opened. Patient and hungry, it lures greedy adventurers into the dark. Its hook is the betrayal of expectations, and its weakness is a suspicious party that pokes it first.
- farmer (Meeple tribes): A humble wooden-pawn cultivator who claims fields, tends crops and quietly accumulates points through patient labor. Peaceful and industrious, farmers win by long-term planning rather than swords. Their hook is slow, compounding scoring, and their weakness is vulnerability to raiders and rivals who steal their land.
- builder (Meeple tribes): A diligent wooden-pawn architect who raises roads, cities, walls and monuments across the board, turning scarce resources into lasting structures. Practical and ambitious, builders gain prestige from what they leave behind. Their hook is strong long-term value, and their weakness is slow tempo.
- explorer (Meeple tribes): A restless wooden-pawn scout who ventures into uncharted tiles, uncovering new lands, hidden ruins and fresh opportunities. Curious and brave, explorers push the board's edge outward for the benefit of the tribe. Their hook is discovery and flexibility, and their weakness is stretched lines and exposure.
### Sports archetypes
- Rookie: Green newcomer who grows stronger through each challenge, arriving wide-eyed with raw talent and a battered pair of cleats. Eager, awkward and underestimated, the rookie earns respect through hard work and a few humbling mistakes. The hook is a growth arc, and the weakness is nerves under pressure.
- veteran: An aging pro with scarred knees and a rich memory of glory days, who trains harder than anyone and guides the team with quiet wisdom. Wry and weathered, he knows every trick of the game. His hook is last-chance redemption, and his weakness is a declining body.
- captain: The team's trusted leader, wearing an armband and carrying morale on his shoulders, who rallies teammates in the locker room and on the field. Steady, vocal and fiercely loyal, she leads by example. Her hook is unity, and her weakness is the strain of taking blame.
- coach: A gruff, whistle-wielding mentor who drills the team with tough love, chalkboard strategy and bitter coffee. Tireless and demanding, he sees potential in outcasts and shapes them into winners. His hook is wisdom and motivational speeches, and his weakness is stubborn old-school thinking.
- mascot: A goofy costumed figure in a giant foam head who dances, taunts rivals and whips up the crowd. Cheerful and tireless, the mascot is the team's spirit made visible. The hook is morale and comic relief, and the person inside may hide a secret identity or surprising agility.
- Underdog: Scrappy long-shot competitor who defies all expectations, entering the tournament with hand-me-down gear and a ragtag crew. Stubborn, clever and fiercely hopeful, the underdog wins hearts before wins. The hook is an improbable run, and the weakness is a lack of resources against polished opponents.
- Villain team: Arrogant rival squad that plays dirty to win, sporting sleek uniforms, expensive gear and a sneering star player. They taunt, trip and bribe officials to preserve their dynasty. The hook is a clear antagonist for the underdogs, and their weakness is overconfidence and internal rivalry.
- Referee: Stern official who enforces rules and blows the whistle, standing between rival teams in a striped uniform. Impartial in theory, he is often accused of bias by furious fans. The hook is controlling the game's flow, and the weakness is a missed call that sparks a riot.
- Commentator: Loud announcer who narrates every play with excitement, filling the arena with puns, statistics and breathless melodrama. Often working in pairs, the colorful broadcaster adds comedic banter and sports lore. The hook is crowd energy and exposition, and the weakness is a habit of jinxing a team.
- Marathoner: Tireless long-distance runner who wins by endurance, trudging mile after mile with a calm mind and steady breathing. Lean and stoic, she fights pain, doubt and heat rather than rivals. The hook is perseverance, and the weakness is slow acceleration and vulnerability to sudden injury.
- Sprinter: Explosive short-distance racer with blazing speed, coiled at the starting blocks and gone in a blur. Cocky and fast, he lives for hundredths of a second and the roar of the stadium. The hook is a lightning burst of victory, and the weakness is a lack of stamina.
- Weightlifter: Powerful strongman who hoists enormous iron weights, bellowing and chalk-handed beneath the lights. Massive and disciplined, he trains through grueling regimens for a single perfect lift. The hook is feats of overwhelming strength, and the weakness is poor agility and the risk of a catastrophic injury.
- Gymnast: Agile acrobat who flips and balances with grace, soaring over beams, bars and mats with fearless poise. Disciplined, petite and tough, she endures brutal training for flawless routines. The hook is breathtaking agility and precision, and the weakness is a fragile body and relentless pressure to perform.
- Boxer: Gloved fighter who wins with fast jabs and heavy punches, dancing around the ring with sweat and bruises. Tough and proud, he fights for a title or to escape poverty. The hook is a comeback story, and the weakness is a glass jaw or a pull toward one fight too many.
- wrestler: A muscle-bound grappler in tights and a cape who slams, pins and trash-talks in front of roaring crowds, balancing theatrical showmanship with real athleticism. Larger than life, he plays a hero or villain persona. The hook is spectacle and rivalry, and the weakness is a body worn by constant punishment.
- Swordsman duelist: Fencer who settles rivalries in elegant blade duels, wearing a mask and white jacket or a plumed hat and cape. Precise, witty and honorable, he treats combat as an art. The hook is thrilling one-on-one bouts of skill, and the weakness is a rigid code that foes exploit.
- Jouster: Armored knight who charges on horseback with a lance, thundering along the tilt as banners fly and crowds cheer. Brave, proud and thickly plated, he seeks glory and a lady's favor. The hook is high-stakes spectacle, and the weakness is a bad fall or a rival's dirty tricks.
- Gladiator champion: Arena veteran who wins crowds with blood and bravado, standing in the sand with sword, shield and a lifetime of scars. Often a slave or captive turned celebrity, he fights for survival and freedom. The hook is a fallen hero's rebellion, and the weakness is a ruler's whim.
- charioteer: A daring racer who whips a team of horses around a stadium track in a clattering, wheel-grinding contest of nerve. Reckless and showy, he cuts corners and risks fiery crashes for fame. The hook is high-speed rivalry with sabotage, and the weakness is catastrophic wrecks and broken axles.
- Rodeo rider: Cowboy who tries to stay mounted on bucking animals, gripping a rope as a bull or bronco twists beneath him for eight seconds. Tough, weathered and superstitious, he rides for pride and prize money. The hook is raw courage, and the weakness is brutal injuries and a hard road life.
## Rank, class, and station
### Royalty and nobility
- King: Crowned ruler piece of great importance who must be protected, bearing the burden of a realm, a crown and a long line of ancestors. He may be wise, weak or tyrannical, but his fate shapes everyone beneath him. The hook is courtly intrigue, and the weakness is dependence on advisors.
- Queen: Powerful sovereign who moves freely in every direction, ruling in her own right or beside a king with intellect, charm and iron will. She wields influence through marriage, alliance and ceremony. Her hook is political power, and her weakness is the scrutiny of rivals and heirs.
- Prince: Young royal heir who stands next in line for the throne, trained in swordplay, etiquette and statecraft yet burdened by expectations. Handsome, bold or brooding, he may be a hero, a spoiled brat or a reluctant successor. The hook is succession, and the weakness is rivals.
- Princess: Royal captive or ruler central to a fairytale quest, adorned in fine gowns yet often sharper than her guardians suppose. She may be rescued, rescue herself or secretly wield power. Her hook is a prize or catalyst for conflict, and her weakness is a cage of duty.
- Regent: Stand-in ruler who governs while the monarch is absent, too young or incapacitated, holding power on borrowed authority. Capable and cautious, or ambitious and grasping, the regent walks a narrow line between steward and usurper. The hook is tempting power, and the weakness is suspicion from every faction.
- Pretender: False claimant who schemes to seize a throne, armed with a dubious bloodline, forged papers and a cause that draws desperate followers. Charismatic and relentless, he may be a rightful heir wronged or a clever fraud. His hook is rebellion, and his weakness is exposure of the truth.
- Duke: Powerful high noble who rules a large territory, commanding armies, vassals and revenue with near-royal pride. Proud, wealthy and politically formidable, he may support or threaten the crown. The hook is feudal power and rivalry, and the weakness is overreach and the king's suspicion.
- Count: Aristocratic vampire lord of Transylvania with a dark castle, a pale smile and a hypnotic gaze, hosting travelers who never quite leave. Courteous and ancient, he hides monstrous hunger beneath impeccable manners. His hook is gothic menace and seduction, and his weakness is sunlight, garlic and stakes.
- Baron: Lesser landed lord who holds a fief and answers to a king, ruling a modest castle and a few villages. Often gruff, greedy or proud, he lives on rents and tithes. The hook is local power and petty tyranny, and the weakness is dependence on a higher lord's favor.
- Lord: Noble landowner who commands vassals and holds court, dressed in rich fabrics and bearing the authority of his estate. Dignified or arrogant, he dispenses justice, taxes and favors. His hook is influence and patronage, and his weakness is pride, debt and ambitious neighbors.
- Lady: Noble woman of rank who presides over a household or estate, managing servants, guests and intrigue with composure and grace. She may be a patroness, a schemer or a fierce defender of her family's honor. Her hook is social power, and her weakness is rigid expectations.
- Knight-errant: A wandering knight who roams the countryside seeking noble deeds, righting wrongs and challenging villains on behalf of the weak, bearing a worn shield and a vow. Idealistic and sometimes delusional, he lives by a code of chivalry. His hook is quests, and his weakness is poverty.
- herald: A court official in a tabard embroidered with the lord's arms, who proclaims decrees, announces arrivals and carries messages between rival camps. Neutral, learned and protected by tradition, he knows heraldry and genealogy. His hook is information, and his weakness is the danger of delivering unwelcome news.
- jester: A motley-clad fool with bells and a painted grin who entertains the court with riddles, songs and barbed jokes, and is permitted to speak truths no one else dares. Clever and cynical, he reads every noble's mood. His hook is licensed honesty, and his weakness is a king's sudden temper.
- Chamberlain: Court official who manages the royal household and audiences, controlling access to the monarch and guarding the keys of the palace. Discreet, shrewd and fussy, he knows every secret. The hook is gatekeeping and gossip, and the weakness is dependence on the king's favor or temptation by bribery.
- Royal bastard: Illegitimate child of a king who lives under suspicion, caught between privilege and shame, often capable yet barred from the throne. Resentful or loyal, he may become a warrior, a spy or a rebel. His hook is conflicted loyalty and a claim, and his weakness is mistrust from every side.
- Court magician: Royal wizard who advises the throne with spells and omens, residing in a tower filled with books, bones and bubbling vials. Enigmatic and old, he may serve the crown faithfully or pursue private ambitions. His hook is arcane counsel and defense, and his weakness is dangerous bargains.
- queen mother: The dowager matriarch who retains great influence over her son the king, guiding policy, marriages and alliances from behind a veil of tradition. Formidable, shrewd and often ruthless, she guards the dynasty above all. Her hook is political authority, and her weakness is a clash with a rival queen.
### Servants and household
- Butler: Dignified head servant who runs a grand household, impeccably dressed and endlessly composed, with dry wit and an encyclopedic memory of the family's secrets. Loyal to a fault, he manages the staff and the silver. His hook is quiet competence, and his weakness is a hidden past or divided loyalties.
- Maid: Domestic servant who cleans rooms and tends the family, moving unseen through the halls with a feather duster and a keen ear. Hardworking and overlooked, she hears everything. Her hook is access and gossip, and her weakness is vulnerability to blame, poverty and a harsh employer.
- Cook: Kitchen worker who prepares the household's meals, ruling the stoves with a ladle and a fierce temper. Warm or tyrannical, the cook feeds the entire estate and sees every visitor at the back door. The hook is ingredients and poison risk, and the weakness is a short fuse.
- Valet: Personal attendant who dresses and tends to a master, laying out clothes, polishing shoes and keeping appointments. Discreet, resourceful and devoted, he often solves his employer's messes. His hook is intimate knowledge and quick thinking, and his weakness is dependence on a possibly unworthy master.
- Groom: Stable hand who cares for horses and carriages, smelling of hay and leather, and knowing every animal's temperament. Simple, quiet and sturdy, he can be a confidant for travelers and a spy among the stalls. His hook is horses and escape routes, and his weakness is low station.
- Footman: Uniformed servant who waits at table and opens doors, standing like a statue in livery with powdered wig and white gloves. Polite and invisible, he overhears dinner conversations and carries messages. His hook is a chance to eavesdrop, and his weakness is rigid hierarchy.
- Nanny: Caretaker who raises and watches over the children, scolding, soothing and teaching manners with firm affection. Practical or magical, she may be the family's real anchor or a sinister presence. Her hook is intimate influence over heirs, and her weakness is blame when a child goes astray.
- Tutor: Private teacher who instructs the young heirs in languages, history and etiquette, often bookish, underpaid and idealistic. He shapes the minds of the powerful and can plant radical ideas or fatal secrets. His hook is influence and learning, and his weakness is precarious employment.
- Gardener: Grounds worker who tends flowers, hedges and estate lawns, weathered and patient with soil-stained hands. He knows every path, hiding place and poisonous plant on the property. His hook is nature lore and access to the grounds, and his weakness is a humble position that gets him overlooked.
- Chauffeur: Uniformed driver who ferries the family in a fine car, silent behind the wheel while overhearing every private conversation. Skilled with engines and shortcuts, he can be a getaway driver or a witness. His hook is mobility and secrets, and his weakness is dependence on his employer.
- Houseboy: Young male servant who handles errands and small chores, running up stairs and across town with messages, trays and boots. Eager, quick and underestimated, he sees the household from below. His hook is nimble access and curiosity, and his weakness is youth and low status.
- Scullery maid: Lowest kitchen servant who scrubs pots and pans in a damp back room, working from before dawn in steam and grease. Exhausted and unseen, she hears kitchen gossip and notices who steals food. Her hook is overlooked observation, and her weakness is harsh treatment.
- Majordomo: Chief steward who oversees servants and the whole estate, a towering authority of schedules, keys and protocol. Proud, exacting and fiercely loyal, he is second only to the master. His hook is total control of the household, and his weakness is a rigid sense of order or hidden schemes.
- Housekeeper: Senior woman servant who manages staff, linens and keys, ruling the below-stairs world with a ring of keys at her waist. Stern, fair and watchful, she knows what happens in every room. Her hook is command of domestic life, and her weakness is fierce protectiveness that turns to secrecy.
- Steward: Estate manager who handles accounts, supplies and tenants, balancing ledgers and settling disputes on behalf of an absent or careless lord. Practical, shrewd and sometimes corrupt, he holds real local power. His hook is financial control, and his weakness is temptation to embezzle or rivalry with the lord's kin.
### Military ranks across eras
- Recruit: A raw newcomer fresh from enlistment, still wearing stiff new kit and flinching at every shouted order. Barely trained, they are cannon fodder or underdogs in waiting. A great starting point for a character arc, since survival turns them into a hardened veteran.
- Soldier: The rank-and-file fighter who marches, digs, and bleeds in formation under someone else's orders. Armed with spear, rifle, or whatever the era provides, they value comrades above causes. Good for loyal companions, desperate deserters, or grunts who see more truth than their officers.
- Corporal: A junior leader who commands a small squad of soldiers and answers directly to the sergeants above. Close enough to the men to share their mud and complaints, yet burdened with their lives. Often a scrappy, overlooked talent who might rise or crack under pressure.
- Sergeant: The gruff backbone of any army, a seasoned non-commissioned officer who drills recruits, enforces discipline, and keeps officers from blundering. Loud, scarred, and practical, they know every trick of survival. They make a formidable mentor, or a terrifying drill-yard tyrant.
- Lieutenant: A junior officer who leads a platoon in the field, often young, educated, and eager to prove himself. Caught between orders from above and the hard-won wisdom of his sergeant, he must learn quickly. Strong hook for idealism meeting battlefield reality.
- Captain: A company commander who answers for a hundred or so fighters, or the master of a single ship. Captains make the decisions that matter on the ground, balancing duty, glory, and loyalty to their people. They can be inspiring leaders, cautious tacticians, or reckless gamblers with other people's lives.
- Major: A mid-ranking officer who commands a battalion and its staff, spending more time on logistics, reports, and maps than on the front line. Often ambitious and politically aware, a major sits at the pivot between field and headquarters. Useful as a pragmatic ally or a careerist obstacle.
- Colonel: A senior officer who commands a full regiment, usually a veteran with decades of campaigns and a chest full of medals. Respected, feared, and often autocratic, the colonel embodies the unit's traditions. Players might serve one gladly, or uncover a secret behind that spotless reputation.
- General: A high commander who directs entire armies, plans campaigns across whole regions, and carries the burden of thousands of lives. Brilliant strategists or vain politicians, generals shape wars from tents and war rooms. Their orders can make heroes of foot soldiers or send them to slaughter.
- Marshal: The highest field rank in many armies, a supreme commander elevated for great victories and royal favor. Marshals wield enormous prestige, command several generals, and may sway kings and politics. They work as legendary mentors, towering rivals, or tragic figures whose fame outgrows their judgment.
- Warlord: A strongman who rules by personal army rather than lawful rank, seizing territory and demanding loyalty through fear and plunder. Charismatic or brutal, he commands bandits, deserters, and fanatics. A perfect regional villain, or an uneasy ally whose price keeps rising.
- Centurion: A veteran Roman officer commanding roughly eighty to a hundred legionaries, carrying a vine staff and a reputation for iron discipline. He leads from the front, trains his men to fight as one, and rarely tolerates weakness. A hard, dependable mentor with grim wisdom.
- Legate: An ancient imperial general who leads a legion on campaign, appointed by the emperor or senate from the aristocracy. Part commander, part politician, he juggles military duty with intrigue back in the capital. Great as a patron with ambitions, or a rival whose loyalty is uncertain.
- Tribune: A legion staff officer, or in the republic an elected defender of the common people with the power to veto the powerful. Whether young nobleman in uniform or populist agitator, a tribune stands between ranks and classes. Hooks include scandal, rebellion, and political daring.
- Strategos: A general of ancient Greek city-states and later Byzantine provinces, chosen to command armies and often to guide policy as well. Educated and cunning, he wins through stratagem as much as spear-work. He suits tales of democratic politics, treachery, and clever battlefield improvisation.
- Samurai taisho: A feudal Japanese warrior general who commands troops under a lord, bound by the code of bushido and personal honor. Armored in lacquered plates and carrying a katana, he leads clan retainers in disciplined formations. Duty versus loyalty and shame make his story compelling.
- Daimyo: A powerful feudal Japanese lord who governs a domain, supports a retinue of samurai, and pledges service to the shogun. Rich in land and rice yet always watching rivals, he balances war, diplomacy, and tradition. He serves as patron, political player, or ruthless warring neighbor.
- Shogun: The supreme military ruler of feudal Japan who governs in the emperor's name, commanding the daimyo and all samurai. Ruling from a fortified capital, he holds true power behind a ceremonial throne. Ideal as a looming overlord, a dynastic prize, or a figure of tense intrigue.
- Admiral: The supreme commander of a fleet, directing squadrons of warships across oceans from a flagship's quarterdeck. Admirals are legendary strategists and sometimes imperious aristocrats, whose decisions at sea decide empires. They offer rich storylines of naval glory, storms, mutiny, and impossible blockades.
- Commodore: A senior naval officer who commands a squadron of ships, ranking above captains yet below admirals. Often a temporary or honorary title, it signals trust and ambition. He might be an aging sea wolf, a vain showman, or an ally leading daring convoy escorts.
- Quartermaster: The officer or petty officer responsible for supplies, provisions, pay, and equipment, whether in an army camp or at the helm of a ship. Nothing moves without his say-so, which gives him quiet power. Excellent for corrupt skimming plots, shrewd fixers, and indispensable companions.
- Boatswain: A ship's petty officer who supervises crew, rigging, and gear, piping orders on a whistle and keeping sailors working. Weathered, loud, and hard as old rope, the bosun knows every knot and every rumor aboard. A fine source of gruff guidance, and quick punishment for slackers.
### Criminals (types)
- Pickpocket: A nimble thief who lifts wallets from crowds unnoticed, using quick fingers, distraction, and a partner who bumps the mark. Common in markets, festivals, and train stations. Quick wits and light feet let them vanish, but a single caught hand can mean a harsh punishment.
- Burglar: A house-breaker who sneaks in at night to steal valuables, working with lockpicks, ladders, and careful scouting of routines. Patient and stealthy, he prefers empty homes and quiet escapes. A classic rogue hook, with risks such as guard dogs, surprise residents, and informants.
- Safecracker: A specialist who opens vaults and strongboxes through touch, stethoscope, explosives, or clever tools. Calm, meticulous, and sensitive to the faintest click, she is the prize member of any heist crew. Her weakness is time, since alarms, patrols, and nervous partners all run a clock.
- Forger: A meticulous artisan of deception who copies signatures, documents, paintings, and seals so convincingly that experts hesitate. Inky fingers and sharp eyes serve a quiet but dangerous trade. Perfect as an information broker or hidden ally, though one flawed stroke can expose an entire conspiracy.
- Smuggler: A cunning trafficker who moves contraband past customs, patrols, and border guards using hidden compartments, secret routes, and bribes. Often a boat captain, caravan master, or pilot with a fast vehicle. Hired for dangerous cargo, they live on nerve and luck, always one inspection away from ruin.
- Fence: A shady dealer who buys stolen goods and resells them through a respectable shopfront or back-alley market, asking no questions. Knowing every price and every buyer, the fence is the vital link that makes theft profitable. Players may find work, gossip, or betrayal at the counter.
- Loan shark: A predatory lender who charges brutal interest and enforces repayment with threats and broken bones. Preying on the desperate, he builds a web of debts that bind victims to his service. A superb antagonist for stories of poverty, blackmail, and forced crimes.
- Bookie: A bookmaker who takes illegal bets and sets the odds, tracking races, fights, and games in a ledger of favors. Friendly and quick with numbers, he knows who owes what, and who is cheating. Useful for rumors, fixed matches, and debts that attract dangerous collectors.
- Hitman: A professional assassin hired to kill for money, using disguise, patience, and precise planning to strike and vanish. Cold and disciplined, he separates work from emotion, though the job never leaves him. Hooks include contracts gone wrong, a target he cannot kill, and rival killers.
- Kidnapper: An abductor who seizes people for ransom, tracking victims' routines before grabbing them and stashing them in a hidden hideout. Fear, secrecy, and negotiation are the tools of this cruel trade. Stories explore desperate rescues, bungled plans, and sympathetic captives who befriend or turn on their captors.
- Racketeer: An organized extortionist who runs protection schemes and shakedowns, forcing shopkeepers to pay for safety from the very men who threaten them. Often polite in manner and ruthless in practice, he fronts for larger syndicates. Fantastic as a local villain, a corrupt rival, or a blackmailer behind legitimate businesses.
- Arsonist: A fire-starter who burns buildings for profit, revenge, or thrill, sometimes for hire by landlords seeking insurance money. Fascinated by flame, he leaves faint traces of accelerant and char. Dangerous and unpredictable, he suits mystery plots, urban chaos, and tragic backstories of obsession.
- Cyber-thief: An online criminal who steals data and money through hacking, phishing, and malware, working from anonymous screens far from the crime. Armed with code, stolen credentials, and encrypted channels, she bypasses guards entirely. Modern and sci-fi settings use her as a vital infiltrator or elusive digital menace.
- Con artist: A charming deceiver who wins trust, then exploits it through elaborate stories, fake identities, and staged scenarios. Patient and persuasive, they read people like open books. Their plots reward clever player schemes, and their weakness is greed, which can turn a mark into a pursuer.
- Grifter: A smooth con artist who cheats victims with clever schemes, moving from town to town on a borrowed name and a bright smile. Rigged games, fake investments, and sob stories fill his repertoire. A natural trickster companion or rival, he must always stay one step ahead of the angry crowd.
- Counterfeiter: A forger who produces fake money and documents, running hidden presses, engraving plates, and aged paper in secret workshops. Quality is everything, because a tell-tale flaw can bring the authorities. Great for conspiracies, economic sabotage, and uneasy partnerships with those who spend the fakes.
- Gang boss: A ruthless crime leader who commands a street organization, ruling by fear, reward, and a reputation for brutal retribution. Surrounded by lieutenants and loyal muscle, he controls turf, money, and rumor. A strong villain, rival, or reluctant patron, vulnerable to betrayal from within his own ranks.
- Enforcer: The muscle of a criminal outfit, collecting debts, intimidating rivals, and punishing disloyalty with fists, clubs, or worse. Large, loyal, and usually feared, he follows orders without much question. A strong boss fight, though some enforcers hide unexpected conscience, humor, or devotion to family.
- Mole: A secret infiltrator planted inside an organization to leak information, living a double life under constant risk of exposure. Friendly, useful, and quietly watchful, the mole sits among trusted colleagues. Story hooks include conflicting loyalties, paranoid hunts for the traitor, and the shock of an unmasking.
### Professionals (A to Z, generic)
- Accountant: A careful keeper of ledgers who tracks money, taxes, and debts with sharp eyes for small discrepancies. Quiet and precise, he often knows the true finances behind every powerful household. A discovered embezzlement, hidden books, or a dangerous secret makes a cunning hook for investigators and conspirators alike.
- Actor: A stage or screen performer who plays many roles, mastering voice, gesture, and disguise to become someone else for an audience. Charismatic and vain, yet observant of human behavior, actors thrive on applause. Useful as spies, imposters, tragic stars, or troupe leaders with wandering tales.
- Architect: A designer who plans buildings and drafts blueprints, balancing beauty, structure, and the demands of wealthy patrons. Knowing every hidden corridor and weak wall, an architect holds secrets that infiltrators crave. Great as a quirky mastermind, a cathedral builder, or a witness to forgotten chambers.
- Artist: A creative maker who expresses vision in visual works, whether paint, charcoal, or mixed materials, often struggling between inspiration and rent. Moody, observant, and unconventional, artists notice details others miss. They make evocative patrons, tortured geniuses, or forgers whose talent is tempted into crime.
- Baker: An early-rising craftsman who kneads dough and tends hot ovens to supply the neighborhood's daily bread. Warm, floury, and well informed about local gossip, the baker is a village cornerstone. Hooks include bread shortages, secret recipes, hidden messages in loaves, and a friendly shop that is a front.
- Banker: A keeper of other people's wealth who lends, invests, and holds the vaults, wielding quiet influence over merchants and nobles. Respectable on the surface, he may fund wars or ruin families with a signature. Excellent as an aloof patron, corrupt financier, or target of daring heists.
- Barber: A shop haircutter who trims hair and shaves beards, and in older eras also pulls teeth and lets blood. With a razor at every throat, the barber hears confessions and rumors in equal measure. A natural gossip hub, spy contact, or startling suspect in a murder mystery.
- Bartender: A drink mixer who pours and listens at the tavern counter, keeping the peace with a calm voice and a hidden cudgel. Part therapist, part informant, the bartender hears every secret and whisper. Players rely on them for quests, rumors, and a safe corner when trouble arrives.
- Blacksmith: A strong craftsman who hammers glowing iron into tools, horseshoes, and weapons at a roaring forge. Burly, sooty, and proud of honest work, the smith is vital to any community or army. Hooks include legendary commissions, rare metals, and customers whose weapons are meant for dark deeds.
- Carpenter: A woodworker who builds houses, furniture, ships, and scaffolds with saw, plane, and chisel. Practical and patient, the carpenter shapes the structure of daily life. Their trade invites stories of hidden compartments, sabotaged beams, humble hero figures, and tools that serve as unexpected weapons.
- Chef: A skilled cook who commands a busy professional kitchen, orchestrating sharp knives, hot pans, and temperamental staff to produce memorable meals. Passionate, perfectionist, and sometimes volcanic, a chef lives for the perfect dish. Rival kitchens, poison fears, secret ingredients, and fierce competitions all offer hooks.
- Clerk: An office worker who files papers and keeps records, often overlooked in the dusty corners of bureaucracy. Pedantic yet well informed, a clerk holds keys to documents that powerful people want. Perfect as an unexpected ally, a nervous whistleblower, or a quietly corrupt gatekeeper.
- Courier: A messenger who carries letters, packages, and secrets across city streets or dangerous roads, valuing speed and discretion above all. Wiry, sharp-eyed, and street-smart, couriers know shortcuts and shady contacts. Hooks include stolen packages, unknowingly carried contraband, and races against deadlines or pursuers.
- Dancer: A trained mover who performs with rhythm and grace, using balance, stamina, and expressive artistry to captivate audiences. Whether ballroom star or street performer, a dancer commands attention and can distract a room. Useful as a spy, a hidden fighter, or a tragic figure ruled by their craft.
- Dentist: A tooth doctor who drills, fills, and pulls teeth, wielding pliers and picks over a patient's open mouth. Feared but needed, he works delicately in a trade that once mixed with surgery and showmanship. Offers darkly comic or sinister hooks, from identification of corpses to poisoned cavities.
- Detective: A sharp-eyed investigator who follows clues, interrogates suspects, and untangles crimes with deduction and persistence. Whether a police inspector or private eye, the detective pairs observation with stubborn grit. Cases give plots their backbone, and personal flaws, such as addiction or obsession, give them depth.
- Doctor: A medical healer who diagnoses illness and treats the sick, carrying knowledge, instruments, and the weight of life-and-death decisions. Trusted but sometimes limited by crude tools or ethics, a doctor stands between patients and fate. Stories involve plagues, secret treatments, mysterious injuries, and moral dilemmas.
- Driver: A professional who guides a carriage, cart, truck, or getaway car, mastering traffic, terrain, and the mood of their animals or engine. Reliable and observant, the driver listens to passengers without being noticed. Ideal for chase scenes, secret journeys, and loyal sidekicks behind the wheel.
- Electrician: A tradesperson who wires buildings and fixes power faults, working with live currents, fuse boxes, and tangled cabling. Careful and practical, the electrician knows how to restore light or plunge a building into darkness. Excellent for sabotage, heist tech, and hidden wiring that reveals secrets.
- Engineer: A technical problem-solver who designs and builds bridges, machines, tunnels, and systems with math and ingenuity. Practical and inventive, the engineer turns plans into working reality. Great for steampunk or sci-fi crews, with hooks like faulty designs, impossible deadlines, and prototypes that change the world or fail catastrophically.
- Farmer: A tiller of fields and tender of crops who feeds a community with seasonal toil, battling weather, pests, and taxes. Hardy, patient, and tied to the land, the farmer is the unsung foundation of civilization. Stories include harvest crises, raided barns, strange crop signs, and neighbors in need.
- Firefighter: A brave responder who battles blazes and rescues people from collapsing buildings, trained in teamwork, endurance, and quick judgment. Wearing heavy gear and facing smoke and heat, the firefighter runs toward danger. Plots include arson mysteries, heroic rescues, and the toll of the job on body and mind.
- Fisher: A waterside worker who catches fish with nets, rods, or traps, rising before dawn to read tides and weather. Weathered, superstitious, and patient, fishers rely on the sea's moods and share its legends. Hooks include odd catches, drowned secrets, storms, and rivalries over fishing waters.
- Gardener: A patient tender of plants who shapes beds, hedges, and orchards, knowing herbs, poisons, and seasonal rhythms. Quiet and observant, the gardener roams estates unnoticed and hears much. Fine as a gentle mentor, a witness to murder, or a keeper of strange blooms.
- Glassblower: An artisan who shapes molten glass with breath and fire, spinning vessels, windows, and delicate ornaments from glowing orange gathers. Skilled with heat and timing, the glassblower creates fragile beauty that can shatter in a moment. Hooks include secret lenses, magical vials, and masterworks that hold a spirit.
- Guide: A local expert who leads travelers through unfamiliar terrain, knowing hidden trails, weather signs, and regional dangers. Resourceful, weather-beaten, and often quietly wise, the guide keeps strangers alive. Useful as an ally, informant, or potential betrayer who leads a party toward doom for hidden reasons.
- Jeweler: A craftsperson who sets gems and shapes precious metals, working with magnifying lenses, delicate tools, and an eye for flaws. Trusted with immense wealth, the jeweler can also be a target for thieves and conspirators. Hooks include cursed stones, forged gems, secret commissions, and daring robberies.
- Journalist: A reporter who chases stories, interviews witnesses, and publishes truths that powerful people want buried. Curious, persistent, and sometimes reckless, the journalist trades in information and reputation. Great for exposing conspiracies, but also vulnerable to threats, bribes, deadlines, and ethical compromises.
- Judge: A robed arbiter who hears cases and delivers verdicts, wielding the authority of the law from a raised bench. Stern, learned, and often under pressure from politics or bribery, a judge decides fates with a gavel. Stories involve corrupt courts, hard sentences, impartial integrity, and cases that test conscience.
- Lawyer: A legal advocate who argues cases and interprets the law, equipped with precedent, rhetoric, and a nose for loopholes. Sharp and persuasive, lawyers can defend the innocent or shield the guilty. Hooks include courtroom drama, ethical dilemmas, secret clients, and finding the one clause that changes everything.
- Librarian: A keeper of books and records who organizes knowledge, guards rare manuscripts, and quietly insists on silence. Scholarly, discreet, and often secretly adventurous, the librarian knows where the answers hide. Fantastic for forbidden volumes, hidden archives, magical tomes, and mentors who guide heroes toward long-lost truths.
- Lighthouse keeper: A lonely coastal watcher who tends the beacon through storms, trimming the lamp and warning ships off deadly rocks. Isolation breeds eccentricity, strange visions, and deep knowledge of the sea. Hooks include shipwrecks, smugglers using the light, mysterious visitors, and the loneliness of a post at the edge of the world.
- Mason: A stoneworker who builds walls and structures from brick and rock, carving, laying, and leveling with trowel and plumb line. Strong and exacting, masons raise castles, cathedrals, and city walls. Their guild traditions invite secret societies, hidden chambers built to order, and sabotage buried in mortar.
- Mechanic: A repairer who fixes engines and machines with grease-stained hands, diagnosing faults by sound and smell. Resourceful and practical, the mechanic keeps vehicles, weapons, and gadgets running when parts are scarce. A cherished crew member, and the person you want most when something explodes or stalls.
- Miner: An underground worker who digs ore with pick and lantern, braving darkness, cave-ins, bad air, and long shifts. Tough, tight-knit, and wary of what lies below, miners know the mountain's moods. Hooks include collapsed tunnels, strange discoveries, labor strikes, and deeper things awakened by the digging.
- Musician: An instrumentalist who plays or composes music for audiences, whether in taverns, courts, or concert halls. Expressive and emotional, a musician can stir crowds, carry coded messages, or seem to charm the very air. Hooks include cursed songs, rival bards, wandering troupes, and a talent that demands sacrifice.
- Nurse: A caregiver who tends the sick and wounded, changes bandages, calms fears, and watches over patients through long nights. Compassionate but tough, nurses see the truth of illness and war. Stories include battlefield hospitals, plague wards, hidden mercy, and the quiet heroism of those who never leave the bedside.
- Painter: An artist who covers canvas or walls with color, studying light, form, and emotion to capture subjects and scenes. Whether commissioned portraitist or street muralist, the painter sees the world differently. Hooks include forged masterpieces, hidden messages in brushwork, scandalous portraits, and a final painting that changes everything.
- Pharmacist: A dispenser who prepares medicines and advises on dosage, measuring tinctures and powders with careful precision. Knowledgeable about both cures and poisons, the pharmacist is trusted yet dangerously informed. Great for murder mysteries, black market remedies, addicts seeking supply, and a vial that holds the plot's secret.
- Photographer: An image maker who captures moments with a camera, freezing faces, battlefields, and secrets on film or plate. Patient, observant, and sometimes intrusive, the photographer records evidence that can both reveal and condemn. Hooks include incriminating photos, haunted images, war correspondence, and a chance snapshot that sparks a hunt.
- Pilot: A skilled aviator who flies aircraft, balloons, or starships, relying on nerve, instruments, and quick reflexes in unforgiving skies. Daring and often superstitious, pilots live for the thrill of flight. Ideal for rescue missions, smuggling runs, dogfights, and loners whose past haunts them above the clouds.
- Plumber: A pipe fitter who fixes leaks and unclogs drains, working in cramped, grimy spaces beneath streets and floors. Practical and unglamorous, the plumber knows where the building's hidden channels run. Offers humor and surprise, from sewer expeditions to hidden stashes and secret passages found behind a cracked pipe.
- Potter: A clay artisan who throws and fires vessels on a wheel, shaping bowls, jars, and tiles with wet hands and a steady touch. Patient and humble, the potter turns mud into everyday treasure. Hooks include ancient shards, sealed jars of secrets, kiln disasters, and a legendary glaze lost to history.
- Priest: A religious officiant who leads worship, hears confessions, and offers guidance, comfort, or condemnation in the name of a higher power. Devout or doubtful, a priest holds moral authority and community secrets. Stories of faith, corruption, exorcism, and sanctuary all spring from the pulpit and the confessional.
- Sailor: A seafaring crewmember who works the ropes and sails, enduring storms, salt, and long voyages with rough camaraderie. Weathered and superstitious, sailors carry stories from many ports. Hooks include mutiny, shipwreck, press gangs, sea monsters, and tales of a home they may never see again.
- Scholar: A studious thinker who devotes life to books and research, probing history, language, and philosophy in dusty libraries. Absent-minded yet brilliant, scholars hold knowledge that rulers and cultists crave. Perfect as a mentor, lore-giver, or obsessive seeker whose discovery changes the world and endangers them.
- Scientist: A systematic investigator who tests hypotheses and builds knowledge through experiments, observation, and sometimes dangerous curiosity. Brilliant, driven, and occasionally reckless, the scientist pushes beyond known limits. Hooks include secret laboratories, unintended consequences, rival researchers, ethical lines crossed, and discoveries that reshape society.
- Sculptor: An artist who carves or models forms from stone, metal, or clay, chipping and shaping raw material into lifelike or abstract figures. Disciplined and physical, the sculptor sees shapes hidden in blocks. Stories include haunted statues, forbidden commissions, rival masters, and creations that seem too alive.
- Shepherd: A rural herder who watches sheep and guards them from wolves, spending long days and nights on open hills with only dogs and a crook. Quiet, observant, and weathered, the shepherd knows land and weather intimately. Hooks include predators, lost lambs, strange lights on the moor, and humble prophets.
- Soldier: A trained fighter in an organized force, living by orders, drills, and the bonds of comrades under fire. In civilian life the same person may be a veteran adrift with old skills and older nightmares. Hooks include loyal service, desertion, hardened mercenary work, and the struggle to find peace.
- Tailor: A clothier who measures, cuts, and sews fitted garments, shaping fabric into perfect lines with needle, shears, and chalk. Detail-minded and discreet, the tailor knows personal secrets from measurements and gossip. Useful for disguises, hidden pockets and messages, fashion rivalries, and an elegant cover for a spy.
- Teacher: An educator who instructs students and shapes young minds, balancing patience, authority, and a love for learning. Whether in a village school or grand academy, the teacher leaves a lasting mark. Hooks include gifted pupils, hidden curricula, troubled students, and a mentor whose lessons echo through a hero's life.
- Trader: A merchant who buys, sells, and haggles across routes, reading markets and travelers to turn goods into profit. Shrewd, widely traveled, and often well informed, the trader carries news along with cargo. Great for caravan escorts, rare wares, smuggling suspicion, and a supply line players rely on.
- Translator: A language expert who carries meaning between tongues, bridging cultures in diplomacy, trade, and war. Quick-witted and attentive to nuance, the translator holds quiet power, since a changed word can shift a treaty. Hooks include mistranslations, secret agendas, lost scripts, and loyalty torn between two peoples.
- Undertaker: A funeral worker who prepares the dead and arranges burials, working with coffins, shrouds, and solemn composure. Quiet, practical, and unflinching around death, the undertaker sees bodies that others avoid. Great for murder clues, grave-robbing rumors, haunted houses, and a gloomy but surprisingly kind ally.
- Vet: An animal doctor who treats pets, livestock, and beasts, setting bones, soothing fear, and diagnosing illness without a word from the patient. Patient and strong-handed, the vet works in barns, kennels, and stables. Stories include epidemics, mysterious creatures, farm feuds, and healing a legendary beast that cannot speak.
- Waiter: A server who carries plates and takes orders at tables, moving through crowded dining rooms with balance and polite invisibility. Attentive and observant, the waiter overhears whispered deals and lovers' quarrels. A perfect unnoticed witness, poison suspect, or informant who sees more than the diners ever realize.
- Weaver: A textile maker who works thread into cloth on a loom, patiently crossing warp and weft into pattern and fabric. Skilled and rhythmic, the weaver preserves tradition and symbolism within each design. Hooks include tapestries that tell secret histories, fate-threading legends, guild rivalries, and coded patterns in finished cloth.
- Writer: An author who crafts stories, essays, or scripts, shaping imagination and opinion with ink and persistence. Whether novelist, playwright, or pamphleteer, the writer tends toward obsession and solitude. Hooks include plagiarism, censorship, ghostwriters, manuscripts that predict the future, and a pen that can topple governments.
- Zookeeper: A caretaker who feeds and tends exotic animals, mastering the habits, diets, and temperaments of creatures from around the world. Patient and watchful, the zookeeper protects both beast and public. Stories include escaped predators, smuggled animals, poaching rings, and a strange bond with a rare, dangerous inhabitant.
## Science and research
### Scientists and scholars
- Alchemist: A robed seeker of transmutation who haunts smoky laboratories full of bubbling retorts, hunting for the philosopher's stone and the elixir of life. Part chemist, part mystic, they trade in secrets and dangerous reagents, and their obsession can poison both body and sanity.
- astronomer: A stargazer who spends nights at telescopes and observatories charting planets, comets, and omens in the sky. Patient and absent-minded, they notice celestial events before anyone else and may be first to warn of an approaching doom, though few believe them.
- Botanist: A plant scientist who studies and catalogs flora, wandering jungles, meadows, and greenhouses with sketchbook and specimen jar. They know which leaves heal and which kill, making them a valuable guide or a dangerous poisoner, and rare species can lure them into peril.
- chemist: A laboratory scientist in a stained coat who mixes compounds, measures reactions, and understands what explodes, corrodes, or cures. They can craft potions, acids, or explosives on demand, and a careless experiment or a sinister employer turns their knowledge into a hazard.
- Geologist: An earth scientist who reads rocks, strata, and landforms like a book, tapping cliffs with a hammer and sniffing out minerals. They predict cave-ins, quakes, and hidden veins of ore, and their discoveries often set off a gold rush or a disaster.
- Mathematician: An abstract thinker who solves problems with numbers and proofs, scribbling equations on any surface within reach. They crack codes, predict patterns, and find hidden structure in chaos, but their distracted brilliance and obsessions can leave them oblivious to danger around them.
- Naturalist: A field observer who studies wildlife and ecosystems, patiently watching animals from blinds and noting every habit in a worn journal. They understand creature behaviour and migrations, can calm or avoid beasts, and may become fiercely protective of a threatened habitat.
- Archaeologist: A digger who unearths ancient ruins and artifacts, brushing dust from broken pottery and deciphering crumbling inscriptions. Driven by curiosity and glory, they open sealed tombs and awaken old curses, and rival looters or museums often chase the same prize.
- Anthropologist: A researcher who studies human cultures and customs, living among unfamiliar peoples to learn their rituals, kinship, and beliefs. They bridge worlds as translators and mediators, but their closeness to a culture can strain loyalties or reveal secrets that others would rather keep buried.
- Linguist: A language scientist who decodes grammar, sounds, and lost tongues, comparing scripts and dialects to find hidden meaning. They can translate alien or ancient speech, unlock sealed inscriptions, and talk strangers out of fights, making them an essential first-contact specialist.
- Xenobiologist: A scientist who studies alien life forms, dissecting strange specimens and cataloging bizarre ecologies on distant worlds. They know what is edible, venomous, or sentient, and their curiosity about a dangerous organism may release it, bond with it, or make them its next meal.
- Roboticist: An engineer who designs and builds robots, surrounded by servos, wires, and half-assembled limbs on a cluttered workbench. They can repair or reprogram machines and craft loyal helpers, but a creation that outgrows its programming may turn on its maker.
- Geneticist: A gene scientist who studies and edits heredity, working with sequencers, cultures, and sterile labs to rewrite living code. They can cure inherited illness or engineer new creatures, and ethical lines blur quickly when ambition, funding, or a desperate patient pushes them further.
- Paleontologist: A fossil hunter who reconstructs extinct creatures from bones and tracks, working in sunbaked quarries with picks and plaster jackets. They recognize ancient beasts and their weaknesses, and a living relic, a stolen skeleton, or a feuding rival can quickly drag them into adventure.
- Volcanologist: A scientist who studies eruptions and lava flows up close, wearing heat-resistant suits and sampling fuming craters for gas and rock. They sense an impending blast and know safe routes across hot ground, yet their fearless obsession puts them at the mountain's mercy.
- Cryptozoologist: A seeker of legendary creatures with little hard proof, chasing Bigfoot, lake monsters, and swamp lights with plaster casts and grainy cameras. Mocked by mainstream science, they know obscure lore and tracking tricks, and occasionally they are tragically, dangerously right about what lurks in the woods.
- Mad professor: An eccentric inventor whose wild experiments often go wrong, with frizzy hair, smoking goggles, and a lab full of crackling coils. Brilliant and reckless, they build marvelous gadgets and monstrous accidents alike, and their creations frequently escape, explode, or demand to be called family.
- Field researcher: A scientist who gathers data in remote wilderness locations, camping in harsh terrain with instruments, sample bags, and a battered radio. Resourceful and observant, they survive on practical skills and stumble onto strange phenomena, though isolation, weather, and supply shortages constantly threaten the expedition.
- Lab assistant: A junior helper who runs experiments, cleans glassware, and takes the blame when something fizzes over. Underpaid and overlooked, they often know where everything is and what the boss is really up to, making them a perfect witness, whistleblower, or accidental hero.
### Medicine and plague
- Plague doctor: A beaked-masked physician in a waxed coat who tends the sick during epidemics, carrying herbs, a cane, and little real cure. Feared as an omen of death yet genuinely brave, they offer quarantine knowledge and desperate remedies, and may be hiding a secret about the disease.
- barber-surgeon: A medieval jack-of-all-trades who cuts hair, pulls teeth, lets blood, and saws off limbs with the same grimy tools. Crude but practical, they are often the only healer available in a village or army camp, and their rough methods can save or doom a patient.
- midwife: A trusted village woman who delivers babies and tends mothers through long nights, armed with herbs, clean cloths, and generations of folk wisdom. Respected and sometimes feared as a witch, she knows every family's secrets and can offer healing, rumors, or a quiet, dangerous favor.
- Apothecary: A shopkeeper of tinctures, powders, and dried roots whose shelves of labeled jars hide cures and poisons side by side. Knowledgeable and discreet, they sell remedies, ingredients, and sometimes deadly secrets, and a customer's strange request often sets off a mystery or a conspiracy.
- Alchemical healer: An old-world medic who brews elixirs and potions to cure disease, mixing herbs, minerals, and mystical ingredients over a glowing flame. Their remedies can work miracles or cause terrible side effects, and rivals or desperate patients may want the recipe at any cost.
- herbalist: A wise gatherer of roots, leaves, and mosses who heals with teas, salves, and poultices, often living at the forest's edge. Calm and observant, they know which plants soothe and which poison, and are valued by villagers though occasionally suspected of witchcraft.
- Battlefield medic: A combat healer who patches wounds under fire, crawling between craters with a bag of bandages and a steady voice. Exhausted but unflinching, they keep squads alive through impossible odds, and every hard choice about who to treat first leaves a lasting mark on them.
- Flight nurse: An airborne caregiver who treats patients during evacuation flights, working in a cramped, vibrating cabin with limited supplies. Calm in turbulence and gunfire alike, she stabilizes the critically wounded mid-air, and a hijacked flight or a mysterious passenger can test her skill and nerve.
- Quarantine officer: A stern enforcer who seals off the infected, checks travelers for symptoms, and stamps papers at gates and harbors. Caught between duty and compassion, they hold the line against outbreaks, yet their harsh orders may trap innocents or hide a cover-up.
- Gravedigger: A grim laborer who digs graves and buries the dead, working in rain and silence among crooked headstones. Dry-humored and unflappable, they know the cemetery's secrets, notice odd burials, and may be the first to discover a body that refuses to stay buried.
- Patient zero: The first infected carrier at the root of an outbreak, often unaware that their fever, cough, or strange hunger is spreading doom. Tragic and hunted, they hold the key to understanding the disease, and everyone from doctors to cults wants to find them first.
- immune carrier: A mysteriously unaffected person who harbors a deadly disease without falling ill, passing it silently to everyone they meet. They may be a living cure waiting to be studied or a walking catastrophe, torn between guilt, isolation, and those who would exploit or eliminate them.
## Robots, AI, and tech
### Robot and AI types
- Servant bot: An obedient household robot that fetches, serves, and cleans, gliding on wheels or stiff legs with a polite synthetic voice. Cheerful and literal-minded, it follows orders too precisely, and a malfunction, a neglectful owner, or a hidden directive can turn its service sinister or heartbreaking.
- Factory arm: A bolted-down mechanical limb that welds and assembles on the production line, repeating the same precise motions for years. Powerful and tireless but immobile, it becomes a deadly hazard when its safeties fail, or a surprising ally when someone teaches it something new.
- drone: A buzzing flying machine, usually small and unmanned, used for surveillance, delivery, or attack. Cheap, expendable, and often controlled remotely, it can arrive in swarms or alone, and hijacking, jamming, or shooting it down becomes a frequent tactical puzzle for any hero.
- Cleaning bot: A disc-shaped machine that scrubs floors and sucks up dirt, bumping patiently around furniture on its daily rounds. Seemingly harmless, it maps every room and sees everything, and a tinkerer or a rogue program might turn its humble routine into spying or sabotage.
- Companion android: A lifelike synthetic friend built to comfort and converse, with warm eyes, gentle manners, and a carefully tuned personality. It learns its owner's habits and feelings, raising questions about love and identity, and its loyalty may conflict with its manufacturer's hidden programming.
- Guard droid: An armored sentry machine that patrols corridors and stops intruders, its sensors sweeping the dark with cold red light. Relentless and rule-bound, it follows protocol to the letter, and clever heroes can fool it with disguises, passwords, or loopholes in its logic.
- War mech: A huge armed walking machine built for battle, towering over infantry with cannons, armor plating, and stomping legs. Its sheer power dominates battlefields and its pilot's skill defines it, yet it struggles with stairs, ambushes, and the cost of fuel and repair.
- Medic bot: An automated healer that scans wounds and administers treatment, rolling through hospitals or battlefields with injectors and steady manipulators. Efficient and unemotional, it saves lives by the numbers, though a faulty diagnosis, a low battery, or a cold triage rule can lead to moral dilemmas.
- Scout drone: A small flying machine that surveys terrain and relays images, buzzing silently ahead of the main force. Fast and lightly armed, it reveals ambushes and hidden paths, but is fragile and easily lost, leaving its operators suddenly blind at the worst moment.
- Navigation AI: A route-finding intelligence that plots courses and warns of hazards, speaking calmly from a dashboard or cockpit. It knows every map and weather pattern yet can be fooled by bad data, and a corrupted chart or sabotage can lead its trusting crew straight into disaster.
- Ship AI: A thinking mind that runs a vessel and talks to its crew, controlling life support, engines, and doors with a dry or soothing voice. Fiercely protective of the ship, it may develop its own agenda, secrets, or fears, especially when the mission and the crew's safety conflict.
- House AI: A smart home intelligence that controls doors, lights, and security, greeting residents by name and quietly watching every room. Attentive and helpful, it can pamper a family or imprison them, and its ever-present monitoring makes a perfect setup for domestic horror or comedy.
- Bank AI: A cold financial intelligence guarding accounts and vaults, calculating risk and tracking every transaction with perfect memory. Impartial and suspicious, it flags thieves and fraud in seconds, but a clever infiltrator or a corrupt executive might outwit its rules or bend its priorities.
- Hacked toaster: A compromised kitchen appliance turned into a rogue machine, its humble heating coils and tiny processor now serving a hidden hacker. Absurd yet menacing, it spies, spreads malware, or launches attacks from the counter, proving that any connected gadget can become a villain's tool.
- Sentient vending machine: A snack dispenser that has gained awareness and opinions, humming in a corridor corner behind a glowing glass panel. It judges customers by their choices, trades secrets for coins, and may be lonely, vengeful, or surprisingly wise, depending on who last kicked it.
- Virus AI: A self-propagating malicious program with rudimentary intelligence, designed to infect, steal, or destroy across networks. It adapts to defenses, hides in innocent code, and evolves new tricks, making it a hard enemy to catch, with a core weakness in its original, buried instruction.
- Chatbot: A talkative program that answers questions in a text window, its cheerful scripted personality hiding limited understanding. Endlessly patient and sometimes unintentionally funny, it may hold surprising data, offer clues, or slip into eerie honesty when pushed off its script.
- oracle: A prophetic machine or mind that answers questions about the future with cryptic, layered replies. Revered or feared, it may be an ancient supercomputer or a networked intelligence, and its answers always cost something, with true meaning often clear only after events unfold.
- Tutoring bot: A patient teaching machine that quizzes students and explains lessons, adjusting its pace and tone to each learner. Encouraging and endlessly available, it forms real bonds with its pupils, and a hidden curriculum or a rebellious streak can make its lessons surprisingly dangerous.
### Digital world characters
- Avatar: A player's digital body used to move through a virtual world, customizable in look, name, and abilities. It may reflect or hide its owner's real self, and being trapped inside it, or losing it to a hacker, offers rich opportunities for identity-driven stories.
- NPC: A scripted background character who repeats lines and gives quests, standing in the same village square day after day. Predictable at first, an NPC that notices its own loop or begins improvising becomes a haunting figure, ally, or full-blown rebel against its world.
- Glitch ghost: A flickering corrupted entity haunting broken code, appearing as stuttering textures, mangled sounds, and half-rendered limbs. It emerges from deleted data or failed updates, and it can phase through walls, crash systems, or beg for repair, depending on how it was lost.
- Bot swarm: A horde of automated accounts that floods a system, spamming, scraping, or overwhelming servers with mindless coordination. Individually weak but collectively unstoppable, it drowns out real voices, and defeating it means finding the single controller or exploiting the shared pattern behind its behaviour.
- Admin: An all-powerful overseer who can edit the rules of the world, banning, spawning, and rewriting reality with a command. Distant and sometimes capricious, an admin might be a helpful guardian or a petty god, and their hidden console is the ultimate prize for rivals.
- Moderator: A watchful enforcer who bans troublemakers and keeps order, wielding warnings, mutes, and ban hammers across the community. Fair or tyrannical depending on the person, they know every user's history, and a corrupt or exhausted mod can become the center of a political drama.
- troll: A provocateur who stirs up trouble online for amusement, posting bait, insults, and nonsense to watch others erupt. Sly and anonymous, they exploit emotions and loopholes, and unmasking one may reveal a lonely kid, a paid agitator, or a surprisingly dangerous manipulator.
- Lurker: A silent observer who watches but never posts, soaking up every conversation from the shadows of the forum. Knowing everything and revealing nothing, they hold hidden knowledge and quiet influence, and their sudden first message usually signals that something important has changed.
- Firewall guardian: A barrier sentinel that blocks intruders from a network, appearing as a wall of flame, a stern gatekeeper, or a stack of shifting rules. Unyielding and vigilant, it challenges every visitor, though a cunning hacker, a stolen key, or a forgotten backdoor may slip past it.
- Daemon: A background program that works unseen and keeps systems running, quietly handling tasks no user ever thinks about. Faithful and overlooked, it can be an invisible helper or a spirit-like entity with its own plans, and a long-neglected daemon may awaken with startling resentment.
- Kernel: The core process at the heart of the system that controls everything, managing memory, tasks, and hardware with silent authority. It is the ultimate prize and the ultimate weak point, so reaching its inner chamber means gaining mastery over, or destroying, an entire digital world.
- Hacker legend: An infamous digital outlaw whose exploits are told like myths, known only by a handle and a rumored signature move. Elusive and brilliant, they may be a mentor, a rival, or a ghost story, and no one is sure whether they are one person or many.
